articles.title: Bankfull and Beyond: Identifying Longitudinally Persistent Reach‐Scale River Corridor Features From Topography
articles.titleEn: Bankfull and Beyond: Identifying Longitudinally Persistent Reach‐Scale River Corridor Features From Topography
articles.abstract: The dynamic interaction of fluvial processes and channel form creates nested, longitudinally persistent landforms such as bars, river banks, and floodplains that are critical for river corridor characterization and modeling. However, these river corridor features remain difficult to consistently and objectively identify at scale. Here we present a semi‐automated, terrain‐based approach to identify and map longitudinally persistent landforms using the INFLection‐based Elevations from Channel Topography (INFLECT) method. INFLECT identifies the elevation of persistent topographic features based on changes in lateral topographic slope (i.e., inflections) from cross‐section geometry, and then aggregates these inflections over cross‐sections to represent reach‐scale conditions. We apply INFLECT to six total reaches from two rivers with diverse channel forms and compare the results to other lines of evidence including aerial imagery, flow recurrence, and hydraulic modeling. We identify baseflow channels, active channels, top of banks, and floodplains, although not every type of feature is detectable in each reach or each cross‐section. Topographic features were most clearly distinguished in alluvial reaches with uniform, well‐defined banks and expansive floodplains; however, innovations built into our method also enabled feature identification in highly confined or bedrock channels where topographic features were less continuous or defined. The freely available INFLECT tool enables semi‐automated topographic river corridor characterization, with implications for hydrologic research, management, and applications.

articles.title: DamSustain: A Flexible Framework for Large‐Scale Vector‐Based Modeling and Direct Reservoir Optimization
articles.titleEn: DamSustain: A Flexible Framework for Large‐Scale Vector‐Based Modeling and Direct Reservoir Optimization
articles.abstract: Reservoirs affect the global water cycle, yet their optimization is hindered by simplified modeling frameworks. Earlier methods typically optimize parameters outside a river model by treating dams as isolated spatial nodes. In these setups, reservoir inflows are calculated by adding time‐lagged outflows from upstream to static local contributions extracted from pre‐simulated flows. While efficient for reservoir‐level objectives like hydropower, this node‐to‐node approach ignores physical routing within river reaches, missing the reach‐scale variables that determine downstream flow patterns. Here, we present DamSustain, a framework integrating satellite‐informed reservoir models and an optimization module directly into the mizuRoute river model. By resolving river dynamics throughout the optimization phase, DamSustain allows reach‐based objectives, such as maintaining natural flow variability, to directly guide reservoir management. We evaluated this framework in the Yangtze River basin by optimizing 19 large hydropower dams against a benchmark node‐based setup. Results show that DamSustain increases total hydropower generation by 4.3% while simultaneously reducing downstream flow alteration by 2.7% relative to a no‐optimization baseline. In contrast, policies derived from the node‐based approach achieve a smaller hydropower gain of 2.3% but inadvertently degrade the downstream flow regime. This divergence occurs because the simplified setup omits channel attenuation and dynamic lateral inflows, generating policies that become hydrologically inconsistent when transferred to the physically routed river. These findings show that explicitly incorporating routing dynamics during policy search substantially reduces this structural mismatch, enabling more physically consistent trade‐offs between energy and environmental benefits.

articles.title: An Integrated Flood‐Road‐Network Modeling Approach for Assessing the Impacts of Urban Storms on Road‐Network Performance
articles.titleEn: An Integrated Flood‐Road‐Network Modeling Approach for Assessing the Impacts of Urban Storms on Road‐Network Performance
articles.abstract: Urban pluvial flooding increasingly disrupts road transportation systems, posing growing risks to urban functionality and societal well‐being. Although previous studies have coupled hydrological models with transportation analysis to assess flood impacts, they commonly represent road functionality in binary terms (i.e., passable or closed) and inadequately account for functional heterogeneity among road segments. This study presents a novel integrated modeling approach that dynamically couples a hydrologic‐hydrodynamic model with a weighted road network analysis model to quantify flood‐induced transportation disruption. By explicitly linking inundation depth to flood‐constrained operating speed at the road‐segment scale and weighted network efficiency at the system scale, the approach enables high‐resolution, time‐varying assessment of flood‐constrained road‐network serviceability. Data limitations in drainage network representation and model validation are addressed through a design‐based drainage network inference module and a crowdsourcing‐based inundation data‐extraction module. Scenario‐based experiments spanning single‐peak storms with varying return periods, durations, and peaking times show that road‐network efficiency dynamics are controlled primarily by storm duration and peaking time, whereas return period determines the magnitude of maximum efficiency loss. The road network is particularly vulnerable to front‐loaded, long‐duration storms with large return periods, which cause abrupt efficiency declines and delayed recovery. Further analysis identifies the inundation‐induced failure of geographically critical road segments as a key mechanism underlying sudden losses of network connectivity. Overall, this integrated approach advances process‐based understanding of flood‐induced transportation disruption and provides actionable insights for enhancing road network resilience and supporting emergency traffic management under extreme urban floods.

articles.title: Evolutionary Particle Filter Data Assimilation With a Complex Process‐Based Hydrologic Model for Enhancing Streamflow Prediction
articles.titleEn: Evolutionary Particle Filter Data Assimilation With a Complex Process‐Based Hydrologic Model for Enhancing Streamflow Prediction
articles.abstract: Accurate streamflow prediction remains fundamental for water resources management, flood forecasting applications, and climate adaptation strategies. Physics‐based hydrological models provide process understanding and spatial transferability, yet uncertainties in model structure, initial conditions, parameter values, and meteorological inputs limit prediction reliability. Data assimilation is a widely used strategy for improving model predictions by constraining model states with observational information. This research develops and evaluates a data assimilation approach, integrating the Evolutionary Ensemble Particle Filter with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (EPFM) with the Structure for Unifying Multiple Modeling Alternatives (SUMMA) process‐based hydrological modeling system across 66 northeastern United States watersheds. This ensemble approach manages computational complexities of particle communication during evolutionary operations, implementing global synchronization protocols at each timestep with coordinated memory management among ensemble members. The system executes data assimilation, updating critical state variables including soil moisture, snow water equivalent, and canopy storage through the assimilation of daily streamflow observations within hourly model execution cycles. Evaluation results show substantial performance enhancements, with 94% of the watersheds demonstrating improved streamflow simulations in terms of Coefficient of determination. The Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency and Kling–Gupta Efficiency improved in 95.5% and 86.4% of the watersheds, respectively. The research demonstrates that the EPFM method is a viable strategy to improve the accuracy of streamflow simulation in a complex process‐based hydrological model, while also providing critical understanding of parameter‐state variable relationships and temporal resolution effects, offering potential benefits for hydrologic process model applications, including watershed studies, monitoring and forecasting.

articles.title: Causal drivers of Alpine flood variability from 1300 to 2005 revealed by climate time series analysis
articles.titleEn: Causal drivers of Alpine flood variability from 1300 to 2005 revealed by climate time series analysis
articles.abstract: Understanding flood variability in the European Alps is critical for risk management, yet causal mechanisms linking climate drivers to floods remain unclear. Previous studies have largely relied on correlations, limiting causal attribution. Here we apply a constraint-based causal inference framework using the PC-stable algorithm, combined with bootstrap stability analysis and Granger causality validation, to multi-centennial climate and flood proxy records from the Hasli-Aare catchment (1300–2005 CE). Our results reveal that total solar irradiance modulates summer atmospheric circulation, notably the summer North Atlantic Oscillation, which causally influences Alpine flood frequency. These relationships are strongest during the Pre-Industrial period (1300–1849) and weaken in the Industrial period (1850–2005), indicating a shift in dominant flood drivers. Our study demonstrates the utility of causal inference methods in paleoclimate research and offers a framework for investigating changes in the drivers of hydrological extremes, important for climate attribution and risk assessment in mountain environments.

articles.title: Physically anchored multi-resolution neural operator framework for flood inundation prediction
articles.titleEn: Physically anchored multi-resolution neural operator framework for flood inundation prediction
articles.abstract: Accurate flood inundation modeling using high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations is computationally demanding, limiting their use for large-scale analysis and rapid scenario evaluation. Although machine learning surrogates have been developed, many struggle to reproduce the full spatiotemporal evolution of flood dynamics while maintaining physically meaningful behavior across spatial scales. In particular, simultaneously capturing basin-scale wave propagation and fine-scale inundation boundaries remains challenging. This study presents a multi-resolution deep learning framework for rapid shallow water equation surrogate emulation of flood depth and extent fields. The approach combines a coarse-resolution neural operator that captures large-scale hydrodynamic behavior with a terrain-aware refinement module that reconstructs fine-scale inundation boundary structure. The framework is trained on high-fidelity two-dimensional shallow-water simulations and evaluated across riverine, dam-break, and complex floodplain systems, including tests under structured bathymetric uncertainty. Results demonstrate accurate reconstruction of continuous water depth fields, wet–dry delineation, and peak flood magnitude and timing. The model closely reproduces the evolution of domain-integrated water volume over time, providing a volume-consistency diagnostic beyond purely geometric agreement, and maintains probabilistic consistency when input topography is uncertain. The framework therefore provides high-resolution surrogate predictions of solver-generated flood depth and extent fields at substantially reduced computational cost relative to direct high-resolution simulation. These findings show that multi-resolution deep learning can efficiently emulate solver-generated hydrodynamic flood responses with strong depth and boundary accuracy and robustness to geometric uncertainty, supporting scalable flood hazard assessment and rapid scenario evaluation.

articles.title: Kinetic partitioning with effective mass accommodation for secondary organic aerosol simulations in chemical transport modeling
articles.titleEn: Kinetic partitioning with effective mass accommodation for secondary organic aerosol simulations in chemical transport modeling
articles.abstract: Secondary organic aerosols (SOA) can adopt liquid, amorphous semi-solid, or glassy solid states in the atmosphere. Previous model simulations have revealed that SOA adopt semisolid or glassy solid phase states over dry regions and in the upper troposphere. A highly viscous phase state in SOA particles can cause kinetic limitations in SOA partitioning, challenging traditional SOA treatments with equilibrium partitioning in chemical transport modeling. In this study, we develop a method to simulate kinetic partitioning of SOA accounting for the impacts of SOA phase state by utilizing effective mass accommodation coefficient ( α eff ). This method effectively accounts for the effects of gas-phase diffusion, represented by the condensation sink, as well as particle phase state and the associated kinetic limitations on partitioning. We initially test this method in box modeling to calculate equilibration timescales of SOA partitioning for a wide parameter space for bulk diffusivity, volatility, and total aerosol mass loading. Comparison with the chemical timestep of 20 min in GEOS-Chem reveals that equilibrium partitioning is still applicable for particles with bulk diffusivity > 10 −15 cm 2 s −1 , whereas kinetic partitioning is required for partitioning of semi-and low-volatile compounds into highly viscous particles. To reduce computational burden, we developed analytical equations with gas-particle mass transfer coefficients effectively accounting for gas and bulk diffusion limitations. The application of the new α eff kinetic partitioning scheme into GEOS-Chem predicts lower SOA mass over drylands (e.g., Western US) in the boundary layer due to kinetically limited growth of viscous SOA particles, whereas SOA mass can be described well with equilibrium partitioning in most other areas at the surface and at 850 hPa. In the upper troposphere at 500 hPa, the α eff -kinetic scheme predicts up to 50 % higher SOA mass as evaporation is suppressed for glassy particles. The developed method is easily applicable, improving description and treatments of SOA in chemical transport models.

articles.title: Joint Bayesian calibration of frontal ablation and climatic mass balance in global glacier models (PyGEM-OGGM-SERMeQ v1.0)
articles.titleEn: Joint Bayesian calibration of frontal ablation and climatic mass balance in global glacier models (PyGEM-OGGM-SERMeQ v1.0)
articles.abstract: Modeling frontal ablation of marine-terminating glaciers is critical for accurately modeling mass change but remains challenging. We present a hybrid, physically consistent and numerically efficient modelling framework that integrates the Simple Estimator of Retreat Magnitude and ice flux (SERMeQ) into two coupled global glacier models (OGGM and PyGEM). The adaptive particle-batch smoother, a Bayesian data assimilation method, is used for joint calibration of all parameters. The coupled framework simulates monthly length changes along flowlines and mass-balance components of individual glaciers. Applied to 71 marine-terminating glaciers across Svalbard during the period of 2000–2019, the model simulates distinct seasonal variations and annual length changes of glacier calving fronts, while reproducing decadal climatic mass balance estimates well. However, frontal ablation tends to be overestimated possibly due to uncertainties in initial geometry and modelled ice velocities. Overall, the good alignment of the regional distributions highlights that the modeling framework, including the efficient joint Bayesian calibration, provides a promising tool for large-scale frontal ablation modeling in glacier evolution models.

articles.title: Respecting the boundaries: balancing climate adaptation and Earth system resilience
articles.titleEn: Respecting the boundaries: balancing climate adaptation and Earth system resilience
articles.abstract: Humans have always adapted to their local climate. Today, human activities are also unintentionally changing the global climate. This will require major adaptations, which cannot replace and must not derail efforts to stop climate change. Yet measures such as cooling buildings or irrigating crops can themselves increase environmental pressures on the Earth system. Using the Planetary Boundaries framework, we combine evidence to estimate the current pressures associated with adaptation to (i) Holocene-like climates and (ii) anthropogenic climate change. Our first-order estimates indicate that climate adaptation currently contributes ∼ 25.6 % of annual greenhouse gas emissions and ∼ 74.1 % of annual human freshwater withdrawals. Climate adaptation even affects the stratosphere: cooling technologies have considerably contributed to ozone depletion. This confirms that climate adaptation currently exerts substantial pressures on the Earth system. Only a minority of these pressures are likely to be driven by anthropogenic climate change; most still result from economic, technological, and population growth and might also have occurred without climate change. But as climate change dramatically increases the need for adaptation, these findings underscore the importance of scaling adaptation in ways that protect people without further destabilising the Earth system.

articles.title: Climate–trait interactions dominate vegetation light use efficiency distributions across China
articles.titleEn: Climate–trait interactions dominate vegetation light use efficiency distributions across China
articles.abstract: Light use efficiency (LUE) is a key parameter in terrestrial carbon cycling, yet its spatial variability cannot be fully explained by climatic factors alone. Plant functional traits are expected to provide important physiological constraints on vegetation photosynthesis, but their roles and interactions with climatic drivers remain poorly understood, limiting the accuracy and improvement of carbon cycle modelling and projections. Here, we use eddy covariance observations from 29 flux sites, together with climate and trait data, to identify the drivers of LUE and map its spatiotemporal variations across China. Incorporating plant functional traits, including rooting depth, isohydricity, leaf nitrogen (N) content and specific leaf area (SLA), substantially improves the explanation of LUE spatial variability from 45 % to 58 %. The attribution analysis reveals that this improvement is mainly contributed by the nonlinear interactions between climatic factors and traits, accounting for 69.1 % of the total importance and considerably exceeding the direct contributions from individual factors. Typically, the SLA-related interactions, particularly those involving rooting depth, temperature and vapor pressure deficit, largely explain tower-based LUE variations in China, suggesting that LUE is regulated by the coordination between vegetation carbon acquisition, soil water access and atmospheric constraints. Based on these findings, we generate a 1 km resolution annual LUE dataset for China spanning from 2003 to 2024. The regional LUE exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity but shows non-significant long-term trends during the study period. Our results emphasize that vegetation LUE distributions are mainly governed by the coupled climate–trait interactions, highlighting the need to represent trait-mediated environmental responses in terrestrial carbon cycle modelling.

articles.title: Forecasting different types of avalanches based on snow depth and snowfall/snowmelt conditions on the southeastern Tibetan Plateau
articles.titleEn: Forecasting different types of avalanches based on snow depth and snowfall/snowmelt conditions on the southeastern Tibetan Plateau
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Reliable avalanche forecasting is essential for protecting mountain communities and transportation corridors, but estimating avalanche occurrence from monitored meteorological and snowpack conditions remains difficult. Operational assessments often rely primarily on meteorological thresholds, although avalanche responses depend on both type-specific triggering processes and snowpack conditions. Using meteorological, pre-event snow depth, and avalanche observations collected during the 2024 and 2025 snow seasons, we analysed 37 recorded avalanche events, together with corresponding non-avalanche periods. Separate logistic-regression models were developed for dry- and wet-snow avalanches using the intensity and duration of the preceding snowfall or snowmelt process and pre-event snow depth. Their performance was compared with otherwise identical models excluding snow depth. Under leave-one-out cross-validation, including pre-event snow depth increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.72 to 0.83 for dry-snow avalanches and from 0.85 to 0.94 for wet-snow avalanches. For wet-snow avalanches, the true-positive rate increased from 0.79 to 0.92, while the false-positive rate decreased from 0.21 to 0.13. These results indicate that pre-event snow depth provides additional discriminatory information beyond meteorological forcing alone, particularly for wet-snow avalanches, and supports the development of locally adapted avalanche assessment methods.

articles.title: Probabilistic neural code for subjective value and metacognition in human cortex
articles.titleEn: Probabilistic neural code for subjective value and metacognition in human cortex
articles.abstract: Subjective value underlies many everyday decisions, yet the neural representations supporting these valuations are inherently noisy and subject to uncertainty. Whether humans have metacognitive access to this uncertainty and how this access is supported neurally remain unclear. Here, we provide converging behavioral and neural evidence that subjective value is represented probabilistically in the human brain. Behaviorally, participants’ uncertainty reports tracked trial-by-trial fluctuations in valuation. Neurally, we decoded probability distributions over value from functional magnetic resonance imaging activity in ventromedial prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortex, and superior parietal lobe and intraparietal sulcus. Decoded neural uncertainty predicted behaviorally reported uncertainty across trial, item, and individual levels. Moreover, predicting behavioral uncertainty required modeling the covariance structure of population noise. These findings indicate that neural populations jointly encode value and uncertainty, extending probabilistic population coding from perception, working memory to subjective value, and providing a neural basis for metacognitive access to uncertainty in value-based decisions.

articles.title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion
articles.titleEn: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion
articles.abstract: Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4 + tumor cells, with CD8 + T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand–receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8 + T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8 + T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8 + T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8 + T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8 + T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4–GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

articles.title: Hyperactive alternative RNA splicing facilitates immune escape in small cell lung cancer
articles.titleEn: Hyperactive alternative RNA splicing facilitates immune escape in small cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: The mechanisms driving cancer immune escape remain incompletely understood. Our study reveals that alternative RNA splicing is hyperactivated in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), particularly in the classic neuroendocrine subtypes, and is associated with poor prognosis. ASCL1 , a defining transcription factor of SCLC, directly binds to and up-regulates the expression of multiple splicing factors, including PRMT5 . Elevated levels of these splicing factors correlate with an increase in skipped exon (SE) events. Notably, the SEs in SCLC exhibit strong immunogenicity and are linked to immune suppression. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PRMT5 significantly suppresses SCLC progression both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptome analyses demonstrate that PRMT5 deficiency reduces the prevalence of SEs and mutually exclusive exons (MXEs), thereby maintaining exons with high immunogenicity. Consistent with these findings, the clinically safe PRMT5 inhibitor GSK3326595 synergizes with anti-PD1 antibody to treat SCLC by repressing alternative RNA splicing and enhancing immune responses. We conclude that hyperactive alternative RNA splicing, which excludes immunogenic exons, serves as a key mechanism for immune escape in SCLC, highlighting a potential therapeutic vulnerability for this aggressive disease.

articles.title: Structural and functional modulation of GluA1 AMPA receptor by type I TARP γ4 and type II TARP γ7
articles.titleEn: Structural and functional modulation of GluA1 AMPA receptor by type I TARP γ4 and type II TARP γ7
articles.abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) facilitate fast excitatory neurotransmission, while their dysregulation is associated with neurological conditions, including epilepsy, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer’s disease. AMPARs coassemble with auxiliary subunits, proteins at the periphery of the transmembrane domain that modulate receptor trafficking, localization, and kinetics. The most abundant auxiliary subunits are transmembrane AMPAR regulatory proteins (TARPs), which are subdivided into type I (γ2, γ3, γ4, and γ8) and type II (γ5 and γ7). Here, we used cryo–electron microscopy, electrophysiology, and molecular dynamics simulations to uncover the mechanisms of GluA1 AMPAR modulation by TARPs γ4 and γ7. We find that the divergent effects of γ4 and γ7 are associated with distinct interfaces between TARP extracellular domains and GluA1 ligand-binding domains, driven by structurally distinct extracellular helix orientation and β-sheet architecture. By completing the TARP structural library, this study provides a framework for understanding how different TARP architectures reshape distinct transitions within the AMPAR gating cycle.

articles.title: Observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from spin ensembles in 2D hexagonal boron nitride
articles.titleEn: Observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from spin ensembles in 2D hexagonal boron nitride
articles.abstract: Hybrid systems consisting of color centers and magnetic materials provide an appealing solid-state platform for advancing the burgeoning quantum technological revolution. Exploring previously unknown coupling mechanisms between optically active spin defects and quantum degrees of freedom is directly relevant in this context. Here, we report observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from boron-vacancy centers in two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) to a proximal ferrimagnet in the near-zero–temperature limit. The spontaneous magnon emission process is overshadowed by thermal magnon effect as temperature increases, reflecting the crossover from a spontaneous-emission–dominated magnon reservoir to a thermally occupied spin bath where absorption and stimulated processes restore balance. By increasing the spin defect density, we further present that spontaneous magnon emission into a common spin bath could help establish magnon-mediated correlations in dense hBN spin ensembles. Our results are quantitatively captured by theoretical modeling, bringing insights into understanding qubit-magnon coupling, correlated spin dynamics, and many-body physics of color centers in the quantum regime.

articles.title: Atomic-scale visualization and assignment of contaminant adsorption geometries at mineral surfaces
articles.titleEn: Atomic-scale visualization and assignment of contaminant adsorption geometries at mineral surfaces
articles.abstract: Directly resolving coexisting adsorption geometries at mineral-water interfaces and assigning them to crystallographic sites remains challenging in environmental geochemistry. Ensemble methods provide population-averaged structural constraints but may obscure minor or similar configurations and do not directly reveal crystallographic registry. Here, we establish an experimentally constrained framework integrating controlled off-axis high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), multislice simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) to resolve crystallographic adsorption registries and corresponding structures. For selenium(IV) adsorption on hematite (001), comparison of apparent selenium positions with multislice simulations accounting for tilt-induced registry shifts supports assignment to iron-iron bridge and oxygen-centered hollow registries. DFT favors monodentate inner-sphere structures compatible with these registries. Extension to lead(II) and uranium(VI) on multiple hematite facets demonstrates the transferability of the off-axis imaging strategy for resolving sparse high- Z interfacial species. This work enables real-space, site-resolved adsorption-structure analysis that complements ensemble-averaged structural methods and provides a basis for mechanistic models of contaminant retention and structure-guided sorbent design.

articles.title: Mantle redox states reveal contrasting styles of late Archean lithospheric subduction
articles.titleEn: Mantle redox states reveal contrasting styles of late Archean lithospheric subduction
articles.abstract: Lithospheric recycling has operated through most of Earth’s history, likely involving subduction since the late Archean. However, the thermal structure and geometry of such subduction systems remain poorly constrained. Here, we quantify the oxygen fugacity ( f O 2 ) of mantle sources modified by recycled supracrustal materials in the North China Craton. By integrating mantle f O 2 estimation, thermodynamic simulation of lithospheric structures, and other geological constraints, we infer two styles of lithospheric subduction with contrasting slab-dip angles. The dominant style shows shallow slab-dip angles, a more reduced arc mantle and a thick overriding lithosphere. The subsidiary, localized style exhibits relatively steep slab-dip angles, a more oxidized mantle source and a thinner overriding lithosphere. In contrast to the prevalence of steep subduction on the modern Earth, flat (or shallow) subduction profoundly shaped the distinctive tectonic evolution of the early Earth, whereas the localized development of steep subduction may have enhanced mantle oxidation and strengthened coupling between Earth’s deep interior and surface environments.

articles.title: Skeletal muscle proteomics reveals metabolic phenotype–specific adaptations to exercise training in health, obesity, and type 2 diabetes
articles.titleEn: Skeletal muscle proteomics reveals metabolic phenotype–specific adaptations to exercise training in health, obesity, and type 2 diabetes
articles.abstract: Exercise training improves metabolic health, including whole-body insulin sensitivity, yet the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We applied proteomics and phosphoproteomics to skeletal muscle biopsies from lean men, and men with obesity or type 2 diabetes (T2D), obtained before and after 8 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) under basal and insulin-stimulated conditions. Before HIIT, protein expression showed a stepwise progression from lean to obesity to T2D. HIIT induced more pronounced proteomic remodeling in obesity and T2D compared with lean men, characterized by increased mitochondrial and decreased proteasomal contents. Phosphoproteomic responses were diagnosis dependent, revealing distinct insulin signaling adaptations. Mechanistically, AMP-activated protein kinase γ2 (AMPKγ2) emerged as a prominent HIIT-regulated protein, exhibiting increased incorporation into AMPKα2β2 complexes across all phenotypes, and AMPKγ2 overexpression in human myotubes increased basal glucose oxidation. These findings elucidate molecular pathways underlying exercise-induced insulin sensitization and suggest AMPKγ2 as a candidate regulator for exercise-induced metabolic adaptation.

articles.title: A divergent bat orthopneumovirus with zoonotic potential constrained by RSV adaptive immunity and broad-spectrum treatment
articles.titleEn: A divergent bat orthopneumovirus with zoonotic potential constrained by RSV adaptive immunity and broad-spectrum treatment
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; genus Orthopneumovirus ) causes severe pneumonia in young children worldwide, yet the zoonotic potential of the few known nonhuman animal orthopneumoviruses remains unknown. Here, we characterized a highly divergent bat orthopneumovirus (BPV) from West African straw-colored fruit bats and established a systematic framework for evaluating zoonotic risk posed by an emerging viral pathogen. Epidemiologic data in bats showed a low viral detection rate (24 of 1778 RT-PCR positive) and low seroprevalence (6 of 66 IgG IFA positive), suggesting BPV episodic circulation potentially sustained in immunologically naïve bats following bat birthing events. Near-complete genomes from two BPV genetic variants revealed prototypic orthopneumovirus organization, but lacked the SH viroporin-encoding gene present in RSV. Functional experiments showed that BPV NS1/NS2 antagonized human interferon β responses, and that BPV pseudoviruses entered human cells (4.5- to 53.5-fold less efficiently than RSV), while being cross-neutralized by human RSV-reactive antisera, together suggesting zoonotic traits that may be partly constrained by cross-protective immunity. BPV escaped neutralization by RSV-specific therapeutic palivizumab and inhibition by lonafarnib, but remained susceptible to MPE8, a broad-spectrum monoclonal antibody that targets the conserved pneumovirus antigenic site III. These findings identify zoonotic traits of a divergent bat pneumovirus while suggesting potential protective value of preexisting RSV immunity and broad-spectrum interventions, which has implications for pandemic preparedness. Whether cross-protection in the human population may change by the advent of RSV vaccination warrants investigation. Efforts to investigate orthopneumovirus host shifts, reservoir studies, and development of broadly reactive orthopneumovirus vaccines and antivirals are warranted.

articles.title: A spatial peroxisomal switch of AGPS drives ether lipid–induced ferroptosis in vascular calcification
articles.titleEn: A spatial peroxisomal switch of AGPS drives ether lipid–induced ferroptosis in vascular calcification
articles.abstract: Vascular calcification is a life-threatening complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet the metabolic changes that cause blood vessels to harden remain unclear. We found that the pathologically enhanced relocation of a lipid-producing enzyme, alkylglycerone phosphate synthase (AGPS), into cellular compartments called peroxisomes acts as a critical driver of this disease. This spatial shift, triggered by the protein PKCη (protein kinase C η), causes a surge in specific lipids that promote cell death and mineral buildup in the vessels. To disrupt this destructive process, we used generative artificial intelligence (AI) to design a custom peptide that blocks the interaction between AGPS and PKCη. When delivered systemically using lipid nanoparticles, this AI-designed therapeutic successfully prevented the enzyme’s excessive relocation, stopped toxic lipid accumulation, and profoundly reduced aortic calcification in CKD mice. Our findings uncover a crucial metabolic trigger for vascular calcification and highlight AI-guided nanotherapeutics as a promising strategy for treating vascular diseases.

articles.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
articles.titleEn: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
articles.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

articles.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
articles.titleEn: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
articles.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

articles.title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang
articles.titleEn: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang
articles.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

articles.title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth
articles.titleEn: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth
articles.abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

articles.title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer
articles.titleEn: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer
articles.abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor–stroma borders harbor a MIF + fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor–adipose borders, featured an FLT1 + endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

articles.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 M w 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
articles.titleEn: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 M w 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
articles.abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude ( M w ) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four M w 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

articles.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
articles.titleEn: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
articles.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

articles.title: Intermediate‐Scale Testing of Multiphase Processes in Subsurface Contamination: Opportunities for Carbon Storage and Land–Atmosphere Exchange
articles.titleEn: Intermediate‐Scale Testing of Multiphase Processes in Subsurface Contamination: Opportunities for Carbon Storage and Land–Atmosphere Exchange
articles.abstract: Understanding multiphase flow and transport in porous media is essential for addressing a wide range of subsurface hydrological, environmental, and earth systems problems. Multiphase processes can involve the movement, trapping, and dissolution of fluid phases within soil pores. Geological heterogeneity across scales—from pore to field—further complicates their behavior. Quantifying subsurface multiphase processes in the field remains a significant challenge. Such data sets are often limited to sparse borehole and well observations; analyses therefore carry considerable uncertainty because initial conditions are poorly defined, natural boundary conditions cannot be controlled, and geological characterization is incomplete at relevant scales. Models validated under these constraints are often site‐specific and not broadly generalizable across diverse geological and climate settings. Intermediate‐scale laboratory testing (IST) complements traditional column and field experimentation by improving fundamental process understanding, refining conceptual models, and supporting model/theory validation under conditions that are impractical or impossible to obtain in the field. IST uses synthetic aquifers with designed heterogeneity that capture key features, allowing researchers to replicate and measure field processes at high spatiotemporal resolution under well‐defined initial conditions and carefully controlled boundary conditions. This paper reviews key advancements in IST, highlighting examples from decades of research on subsurface contamination by nonaqueous‐phase chemicals. It also discusses and envisions how this approach can address current and emerging problems related to carbon storage, greenhouse gas management, and soil‐plant‐atmosphere systems.

articles.title: Disentangling Sources of Uncertainty in Modeling Saltwater Intrusion Due To Sea Level Rise: The Effects of Model Dimensionality, Physics, and Parameter Choice
articles.titleEn: Disentangling Sources of Uncertainty in Modeling Saltwater Intrusion Due To Sea Level Rise: The Effects of Model Dimensionality, Physics, and Parameter Choice
articles.abstract: In coastal aquifers, saltwater intrusion driven by rising sea levels threatens agriculture, ecosystems, and underground infrastructure. Quantifying this process requires numerous modeling decisions that introduce uncertainties; however, most studies only quantify uncertainty due to parameter choices once a modeling approach has been selected. Our goal was to evaluate uncertainties arising from both model and parameter choice when estimating freshwater–saltwater interface movement in response to 1 m of sea‐level rise and various changes in groundwater recharge. We compare four modeling approaches applied to one synthetic coastal landscape with homogeneous (but uncertain) hydraulic properties: a 1D + Analytical sharp‐interface solution, quasi‐2D and quasi‐3D sharp‐interface models, and a 2D variable‐density flow and salt transport model. All numerical models were constructed in MODFLOW 6. Parameter and model‐choice uncertainty were calculated using a Moment‐Based Global Sensitivity Analysis of interface movement at a centroid cross‐section of the coastal watershed. Results indicate that hydraulic conductivity is the dominant source of uncertainty under reduced recharge conditions, followed by aquifer thickness, while the model approach becomes more pronounced under constant or increasing recharge scenarios. These findings highlight the importance of constraining hydraulic conductivity to improve saltwater intrusion predictions. Furthermore, 1D and 2D approaches are limited in capturing out‐of‐plane and regional flow processes represented in 3D models, and simplified 1D + Analytical models reach full intrusion at lower combined hydraulic conductivity and recharge values than density‐dependent models. This study provides guidance for evaluating saltwater intrusion across various modeling frameworks applicable to other coastal watersheds.

articles.title: A Novel Control Volume Method for Flow in Fractured Porous Media on Non‐Conforming Meshes
articles.titleEn: A Novel Control Volume Method for Flow in Fractured Porous Media on Non‐Conforming Meshes
articles.abstract: In this work, we propose a novel control volume method based on the reinterpreted discrete fracture model (RDFM) framework. This method characterizes fractures as low‐dimensional Dirac‐ functions contained in the permeability tensor, making it suitable for conductive fractures on non‐conforming grids without introducing additional degrees of freedom (DOF) on fractures required by other models. Due to the application of the Dirac‐ functions and local mass conservation, discontinuous Galerkin methods were the only methods available that can be used to solve the governing equations. Unfortunately, such methods will result in large DOF and significant computational cost. In this work, we develop the first finite volume method on non‐conforming meshes, assigning only one degree of freedom per cell and discretizing fluxes using the two‐point flux approximation. Numerical experiments show that direct applications of the properties of the Dirac‐ function to calculate the fracture flux may result in false numerical approximations, mainly because the single degree of freedom in each cell cannot effectively represent all the useful information of the fracture. As an alternative, we introduce a new virtual fracture treatment methodology, that is construct two projected fractures intersecting at the cell center in each cell. Then we derive the permeability of the virtual fractures, providing an equivalent representation of the fracture flux within each cell. The validity of the method and algorithm is demonstrated through several benchmark tests and a three‐dimensional case, with comparative analysis showing significant advantages in computational efficiency over existing numerical methods within the RDFM framework.

articles.title: Addressing the Hydrologic Scaling Challenge Using Experimental Hillslopes: 13 Years of Discovery at the Landscape Evolution Observatory (LEO) at Biosphere 2
articles.titleEn: Addressing the Hydrologic Scaling Challenge Using Experimental Hillslopes: 13 Years of Discovery at the Landscape Evolution Observatory (LEO) at Biosphere 2
articles.abstract: The Landscape Evolution Observatory (LEO) at Biosphere 2 has reached its 13th anniversary since the first experiment in 2013. LEO is a large‐scale research infrastructure consisting of three artificial hillslopes with unique measurement capabilities and experimental manipulation. It has been designed as an interdisciplinary community resource for studying the interactions among hydrology, geochemistry, and ecology. In Earth sciences, the hillslope scale marks a crucial scale transition to bring small‐scale process understanding of hydrobiogeochemistry to the catchment scale. This commentary reviews the scientific accomplishments at LEO from a hydrologic perspective and places the key findings into the context of scaling. We demonstrate how LEO can be utilized to address the long‐standing scaling challenge in hydrology, discuss how LEO has advanced the understanding of viable approaches at larger scales, highlight how other disciplines can leverage these conceptual and technical approaches to inquiry, and invite the scientific community to leverage the extraordinary data sets that have been generated through 13 years of experimentation at LEO.

articles.title: Summer land-atmosphere coupling over Europe: a comparative evaluation of observation-based datasets
articles.titleEn: Summer land-atmosphere coupling over Europe: a comparative evaluation of observation-based datasets
articles.abstract: Land–atmosphere coupling has long been recognized to modulate the surface fluxes partitioning in transitional evaporative regimes, where soil moisture anomalies control evapotranspiration. However, globally available in situ observations for these variables remain limited. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of the similarities, dissimilarities, and limitations among gridded observations-based datasets of surface soil moisture, evapotranspiration, potential evapotranspiration, and 2 m air temperature across Europe. The analysis focuses on the IPCC-defined regions of Northern Europe, Eastern Europe, Western-Central Europe, and the Mediterranean during summer (June–August) for the recent 20-year period (2003–2022), and evaluates and compares the representation of land–atmosphere coupling across the different datasets. Results show that while there are relevant differences across datasets in their absolute values and seasonal variations, the interannual variation of the state variables and the spatial variability of land-atmosphere coupling are mostly consistent across the different datasets. The surface soil moisture is the most consistent, showing significant correlations across all datasets, whereas evapotranspiration shows large inconsistency among datasets for Western-Central Europe and the Mediterranean. Some reanalysis datasets exhibit unrealistic annual cycle patterns across variables and regions, which is also reflected in their coupling representation in both temporal and spatial structures.

articles.title: Convolution based techniques for computing self attraction and loading in MOM6
articles.titleEn: Convolution based techniques for computing self attraction and loading in MOM6
articles.abstract: Self Attraction and Loading (SAL), which accounts for the deformation of the solid Earth under the load of the ocean tide and the self-gravitation of the so-deformed Earth as well as of the ocean tides themselves, is an important effect to include in numerical models of the ocean tides. Computing the SAL potential and its gradient is a challenging problem that is often accomplished using the spherical harmonics transform (SHT), but that approach has drawbacks which limit its accuracy. This work employs an alternative approach based on computing the spherical convolution integral, utilizing two implementations of the SAL Green's function, a closed form approximation, and a tabular version regularized by Cesàro summation. The alternative approach is accelerated by the recently developed Cubed Sphere Fast Multipole Method (CSFMM). The convolution technique is implemented in the Modular Ocean Model, version 6, where it provides more accurate tides than those obtained with the SHT when measured against altimetry-based tides. Previous investigators have cited Gibbs phenomenon as a possible source of error in SHT calculations, and these errors, along with aliasing and finite differencing errors, are avoided by the convolution. The convolution approach has different sources of error including errors in the approximate SAL Green's function, quadrature error in computing the convolution integral, and interpolation error from the CSFMM. In addition to comparing the accuracy of the two approaches, we also present the runtime for parallel calculations using up to 1024 MPI ranks.

articles.title: Interactive land in E3SM process-level models: impacts of land–atmosphere coupling in SCM and DP-SCREAM
articles.titleEn: Interactive land in E3SM process-level models: impacts of land–atmosphere coupling in SCM and DP-SCREAM
articles.abstract: Process-level modeling is central to diagnosing and improving atmospheric parameterizations in Earth system models, yet continental single-column and convection-permitting process configurations are often run with prescribed surface fluxes, limiting realism and consistency with fully coupled global simulations. Here we develop, document, and demonstrate a reproducible workflow to enable fully interactive land–atmosphere coupling in both the E3SM single-column model (E3SM SCM) and the doubly periodic configuration of SCREAM (DP-SCREAM). The approach leverages a multi-year offline-forced E3SM/ELM integration to provide spun-up land initial conditions and introduces an offline preprocessing method that generates DP-SCREAM–compatible land restart files by extracting and replicating the appropriate ELM grid cell (including its landunit/column/PFT hierarchy) across the doubly periodic domain, avoiding intrusive modifications to ELM I/O. Using daily-initialized two-day hindcast integrations, we apply this framework to two years over GoAmazon and ten years over the Southern Great Plains, and to targeted short process-level cases (CASS and GoAmazon single/double pulse). Interactive land coupling is required to reproduce key near-surface thermodynamic biases characteristic of global coupled simulations, including warm 2 m temperature biases and the elimination of spurious persistent nocturnal fog layers that arise in prescribed-flux configurations. In contrast, prominent cloud and convection process-level biases identified previously (i.e. insufficient deepening of shallow convection, deficits of mid-level congestus, and weak convective organization) are largely insensitive to prescribed versus interactive surface flux treatments, indicating that they are driven primarily by atmospheric model physics and/or dynamics. These results provide both a community-ready capability for coupled land process-level simulations in E3SM and practical guidance on when interactive versus prescribed surface fluxes are appropriate for process-level model evaluation and development.

articles.title: LCS.jl v1.0: a high-performance, multi-platform computational model in Julia for turbulent particle-laden flows
articles.titleEn: LCS.jl v1.0: a high-performance, multi-platform computational model in Julia for turbulent particle-laden flows
articles.abstract: Multiphase turbulent flow phenomena are observed not only in industrial devices but also in environmental flows, and direct numerical simulation plays a key role in their investigation. Many numerical models have been developed; nevertheless, few models are highly optimized for GPU platforms, which represent the current mainstream in high-performance computing. In this study, we developed LCS.jl (Lagrangian Cloud Simulator in Julia), a single-source and multi-platform multiphase turbulence simulation model implemented in the Julia language and KernelAbstractions.jl. Validation results confirmed that the present fluid and particle statistics agree well with those obtained in prior studies. For GPU execution, the GPU-side prefix-scan implementation reduced the particle communication cost by approximately 88 % relative to the CPU-delegated sequential implementation. LCS.jl achieved CPU performance comparable to the original Fortran implementation, with similar intra-node scaling behavior. For GPUs, strong-scaling efficiency was approximately 70 % up to 256 GPUs, and weak-scaling efficiency was approximately 80 % up to 216 GPUs on TSUBAME4.0 (a GPU supercomputer at the Institute of Science Tokyo). LCS.jl achieved a maximum estimated speedup of approximately 16.3× on GPUs over CPUs. Execution on both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs further supported portability across GPU architectures. A trial heterogeneous execution achieved an approximately 68 % reduction in execution time compared to the CPU-only configuration even in configurations where the GPU was not the primary compute device. These results demonstrate that LCS.jl is a multiphase turbulence simulation platform that achieves both portability and scalability across a variety of computational resource configurations.

articles.title: Climate-related signals in the GV7-C ice core from East Antarctica for 1782–2013 CE: potential relevance to climate and teleconnections between the tropics and Antarctica
articles.titleEn: Climate-related signals in the GV7-C ice core from East Antarctica for 1782–2013 CE: potential relevance to climate and teleconnections between the tropics and Antarctica
articles.abstract: Polar ice cores provide valuable archives of past climate variability, but interpreting these records in coastal East Antarctica remains challenging because multiple meteorological processes can influence the signals preserved in ice cores. Here we investigate climate-related signals in the GV7-C ice core from East Antarctica (1782–2013 CE) using annual records of water isotopes ( δ 18 O and d-excess) and snow accumulation by comparing them with large-scale climate indices and reanalysis-based climate data. Snow accumulation shows strong interannual variability, suggesting multiple and potentially competing controls, and is weakly linked to sea-surface temperature variability over the Indian Ocean sector (1957–2013 CE). δ 18 O exhibits weak but detectable relationships with Pacific-sector variability for 1957–2013 CE, whereas d-excess shows clearer relationships with sea-surface temperature variability in the Indian Ocean sector. Over the longer period (1872–2013 CE), δ 18 O correlations generally weaken, implying time-varying controls, while d-excess retains persistent relationships, highlighting its utility for tracking moisture-source conditions. Overall, the GV7-C record suggests potential teleconnections between Antarctic coastal climate and tropical ocean variability.

articles.title: A comprehensive global ocean radiocarbon dataset (1700–2024) for climate applications
articles.titleEn: A comprehensive global ocean radiocarbon dataset (1700–2024) for climate applications
articles.abstract: Radiocarbon ( 14 C) in the ocean, reported as fractionation-corrected Δ 14 C, is a key tracer of circulation, ventilation, and carbon-cycle exchange on decadal to centennial timescales. We present a comprehensive global compilation of marine Δ 14 C observations spanning 1700–2024, comprising 68 543 measurements from two complementary streams: 58 216 ship-based dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) bottle samples (1955–2024) and 10 327 biogenic carbonate measurements from corals, bivalves, gastropods, and sclerosponges (1700–2020). The ship-based component builds on the Global Ocean Data Analysis Project (GLODAP) by adding data from additional hydrographic cruises and 68 peer-reviewed studies. The carbonate records provide time-resolved observations at individual sites, including historical periods prior to direct measurements, and they extend coverage to coastal, tropical, and deeper-habitat settings where direct seawater sampling remains sparse. All records were screened for metadata completeness, transcribed into a common reporting framework following Stuiver and Polach (1977), and assigned synthesis quality flags (DELC14QC) through primary quality control. Deep-ocean crossover diagnostics are archived separately for user advisory review and do not modify bottle DELC14QC. The merged ship-based and biogenic carbonate measurements together span pre-bomb baselines through the modern bomb- 14 C decline across global ocean basins. Version 1.2026 of the compilation is archived on Zenodo as flat CSV files with a per-contribution source table (Mamnun et al., 2026). The same measurements are available in Linked Paleo Data (LiPD) format on LiPDverse (https://lipdverse.org/, last access: 20 November 2026). The product captures pre-industrial baselines, the bomb- 14 C transient and its penetration into the interior ocean, and the post-peak decline through recent decades, and is intended to support ocean ventilation assessments, Earth system model evaluation, and multi-century carbon-cycle synthesis.

articles.title: Coastal Wetland Restoration and Greenhouse Gas Pathways: A Global Meta‐Analysis
articles.titleEn: Coastal Wetland Restoration and Greenhouse Gas Pathways: A Global Meta‐Analysis
articles.abstract: Coastal wetland restoration is widely promoted as a tool for climate change mitigation, but its effect on the carbon cycle is not well constrained. We conducted a systematic review and meta‐analysis of peer‐reviewed field studies that directly contrasted restored with altered sites, covering carbon stocks and greenhouse gas fluxes across mangroves, saltmarshes, seagrass meadows, brackish systems, and coastal freshwater wetlands. We analyzed 351 pairwise restored versus altered site comparisons from 82 studies. Here we show that restoration increases aboveground and belowground biomass on average, primarily through vegetation establishment at previously unvegetated sites. Soil carbon also increased, both as concentration and as areal stock (sampling depths 2–300 cm), although this effect was not detectable when analyses were restricted to samples from the upper 30 cm. No detectable changes in CO 2 , CH 4 , and N 2 O fluxes (33, 31, and 20 comparisons) were observed, although the available data had the power to detect only large effects. Meta‐regressions detected no significant differences among wetland types, though this result is constrained by unbalanced evidence across systems and studied parameters. The available data are geographically biased toward tropical and subtropical Asia, with minimal coverage in Africa and limited data from temperate and cold coastal regions. Dissolved organic carbon was too rarely reported to be analyzed (nine comparisons from two studies), constraining whole‐system impact estimates. Overall, restoration increases plant biomass on average, whereas the soil carbon and greenhouse gas terms that determine its net climate benefit cannot yet be quantified from the published literature. articles.title: Shared Trajectories in Soil Microbial Succession Across Five Glacier Forefields in the Arctic and Antarctica
articles.titleEn: Shared Trajectories in Soil Microbial Succession Across Five Glacier Forefields in the Arctic and Antarctica
articles.abstract: Glacial retreat exposes new forefield soils for microbial colonization and succession, which shape early soil development and biogeochemical functioning. However, key dimensions of succession—including variation across microbial domains, abundant and rare subcommunities, and soil depths—remain poorly resolved, constraining the ability to predict postglacial successional trajectories and their functional consequences. Here, we integrate measures of taxonomic diversity, phylogenetic structure, and colonist life history traits derived from rRNA metabarcoding data to characterize bacterial and microeukaryotic succession in surface and deep soils across five glacier forefields in the Canadian High Arctic and Antarctic Peninsula. Despite substantial differences in local species pools, process‐ and trait‐based successional trajectories were broadly conserved among forefields. Microbial abundance and taxonomic richness increased over time, rates of community change decelerated as soil conditions stabilized, and turnover was consistently dominated by species replacement. Trait‐based indices further indicated a shift from fast‐growing, spatially widespread taxa towards slower‐growing, more spatially restricted lineages, paralleling a transition from autotroph‐ to heterotroph‐dominated communities. Contrary to canonical expectations of deterministic community convergence, spatial variation among sites and between soil depths increased through time, an effect that was strongly context‐dependent: abundant bacterial taxa converged in membership, whereas microeukaryotes and rare taxa were more strongly shaped by stochastic processes, producing patchier, site‐specific assemblages. Together, our results indicate that microbial succession in polar forefields follows conserved, trait‐mediated trajectories despite underlying taxonomic variability, but diverges from alpine systems in the persistence of spatial heterogeneity and stochasticity. Process‐ and trait‐based approaches may therefore provide more robust predictions of soil development and biogeochemical feedbacks in expanding ice‐free landscapes.

articles.title: Experimental evidence that organo-mineral interactions regulate dissolved organic matter composition and lability across permafrost landscapes of northwestern Canada
articles.titleEn: Experimental evidence that organo-mineral interactions regulate dissolved organic matter composition and lability across permafrost landscapes of northwestern Canada
articles.abstract: Increased land-water connectivity of northern landscapes driven by permafrost thaw is shifting the bioavailability of dissolved organic matter (DOM) in surface waters, with implications for northern food webs and regional and global carbon balances. However, sorption of DOM to previously frozen sediments has received little attention as a mechanism of regulating the bioavailability of organic matter in thaw-affected freshwater ecosystems. Using batch sorption experiments, we assessed sorption potential, water-extractable dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentration, and the impact of sorption on DOM composition of six different permafrost sediment types common throughout northwestern Canada, reflecting variation in geologic and permafrost histories. A principal component analysis revealed that sediment biogeochemical characteristics reflected geologic origin, and past thaw increased within-type variation. Sorption was positively correlated with organo-reactive forms of Al and Fe and negatively correlated with sediment pH. Proportion of bulk sediment organic carbon released as water extractable DOC ranged from 1.0 % to 62.0 %, with yedoma sediments from the Klondike region releasing substantially more DOC than sediments from other regions. Preferential sorption of larger, humic-like compounds and displacement of mineral-bound small, aliphatic molecules enriched the DOM pool in labile compounds. Bio-incubations verified that exposure to sediments increased rates of biodegradation, corresponding with shifts in DOM composition and increased nutrient concentrations. Our experiments demonstrate that organo-mineral interactions have the potential to decrease DOC concentrations while increasing bioavailability of DOM remaining in solution, but that the strength of this response varies with sediment characteristics that are reflective of landscape history.

articles.titleEn: Deep-learning prediction of high-frequency sea-level oscillations in the Adriatic Sea
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: The eastern Adriatic coast is a known hotspot of strong meteorologically induced high-frequency sea-level oscillations, occurring at periods shorter than 1 h and, at some locations, reaching wave heights of several metres. When highest, these oscillations are termed meteotsunamis. In this study, we test deep-learning methods for predicting maximum daily amplitudes of high-frequency ( T JE , extends this approach through joint encoding of atmospheric predictors and a more extensive processing of past sea-level information, with the aim of improving the representation of processes associated with high-frequency sea-level oscillations. Analysis of more than 20 years of data shows that high-frequency sea-level extremes are larger in Bakar (>60 cm) than in Ploče ( JE performs best overall and under regular amplitude conditions, whereas HFNet more effectively captures extreme events, although these remain systematically underestimated in both architectures. Model performance is higher at Ploče, likely because of its smaller sea-level range and simpler response to atmospheric forcing. articles.title: An ensemble groundwater prediction (EGP) system to forecast groundwater levels in alluvial aquifers in Switzerland
articles.titleEn: An ensemble groundwater prediction (EGP) system to forecast groundwater levels in alluvial aquifers in Switzerland
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Groundwater is a key source of freshwater for drinking water supply and agricultural irrigation on a global scale. Groundwater in Switzerland (and beyond) is traditionally regarded as a reliable source of freshwater. Recent extreme drought events (i.e. in 2018, 2022, and 2026) have shown, however, that groundwater responds to these events and can cause problems for water supply and groundwater availability. With hydrological extremes becoming more frequent, there is a growing need for early warning systems and improved forecasting. This study develops and tests a scalable ensemble groundwater prediction (EGP) system with a 32 d lead time. The system combines extended-range precipitation and temperature forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) with the lumped-parameter groundwater model Pastas. Forecasts were evaluated at six monitoring wells across Switzerland, representing diverse hydrogeological settings, and compared to naive persistence and climatology benchmarks. Results indicate that the EGP system produces skillful forecasts up to 32 d ahead, with Spearman correlations between 0.73–0.99 for one to four weeks ahead. The required model–data complexity to provide skillful forecasts varies. In aquifers with long response times and memory, forecasts driven by recent measurements of precipitation and temperature, as well as climatology, are sufficient. In fast-responding, short-memory systems, however, using meteorological forecasts of precipitation and temperature adds clear value and improves groundwater level forecasts compared with using only recent meteorological measurements and system memory. Forecast skill in mountainous regions (e.g. Davos) remains limited because local meteorology is difficult to predict. These findings highlight both the potential and the limitations of short-term groundwater forecasting.

articles.title: Vegetation Greening Modulates Precipitation Pattern in China: Enhanced Moisture Recycling and Increased Atmospheric Instabilities Driven by Land‐Atmosphere Feedbacks
articles.titleEn: Vegetation Greening Modulates Precipitation Pattern in China: Enhanced Moisture Recycling and Increased Atmospheric Instabilities Driven by Land‐Atmosphere Feedbacks
articles.abstract: The land use and land cover change (LUCC) is disrupting the water and energy balances of the land surface recently, thereby modulating precipitation formation through land‐atmosphere feedbacks. However, this effect has not been fully quantified across the nine major river basins in China with distinct natural conditions. In this study, the local and remote effects of the LUCC on precipitation were evaluated using an advanced moisture tracking model. The results reveal that the greening trend of vegetation has enhanced land‐atmosphere feedbacks since 1999, which was mainly reflected by increasing evapotranspiration (ET). This feedback mechanism led to an increasing recycling ratio of precipitation (0.003–0.009 decade −1 ), precipitable water vapor (0.30–1.28 mm/decade) and a general decrease in the lifting condensation level (−181.8 to 43.3 m/decade). Increasing atmospheric moisture also induced a rise (0.1%–9.9%) in the proportion of days with high convective available potential energy values, indicating an increase in atmospheric instabilities associated with increased atmospheric convection and precipitation. Increasing ET moisture from the Three‐North Region increased precipitation in the North China Plain and Northeast China Plain by 4.7–75.1 mm/decade through remote effect, while its contribution to the local and downwind extreme precipitation remained stable under the LUCC. Afforestation in the Yellow River and Inland River Basins has reached the sustainability threshold, while it remains sustainable in other river basins in China. This study will provide a solid scientific basis for supporting the optimization of ecological engineering planning in different basins with diverse climatic and land cover conditions.

articles.title: Process‐Based Modeling Approach for Simulating Rice Paddy Methane Fluxes: Model Evolution, Performance, and Way Forward
articles.titleEn: Process‐Based Modeling Approach for Simulating Rice Paddy Methane Fluxes: Model Evolution, Performance, and Way Forward
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Over the years, an improved understanding of complex biogeochemical processes has led to the development of numerous process‐based models to simulate the factors that affect methane fluxes from rice paddies, thereby playing a crucial role in understanding and predicting them. Process‐based models have demonstrated strong performance in capturing the complexities of rice‐paddy systems, providing a robust framework for capturing the dynamics of processes involved. However, models are still limited by the representation of underlying mechanisms, uncertainties involved in natural processes, the unavailability of long‐term measurement data for validation under various climate and management practices, and gaps in current knowledge. Models are continuously revised and upgraded over time, undergoing several iterations that lead to the addition of new submodules and routines. These additions incorporate new processes and equations, enhancing the model's performance with multiple individuals across organizations working on it. However, this can create confusion, especially when changes are not properly documented, leading to redundancy and repetition that impede research progress. This paper aims to gather current knowledge and provide a comprehensive account of the development, evolution, and performance of models used for simulating methane emissions from rice paddies, thereby aiding the development of future models and their applications. To advance research, there is an urgent need to maintain a record of changes to model versions, make knowledge and source code available for critique and further development, maintain long‐term, standardized, measured data sets for validation and testing using a community‐based platform, and enhance adaptability by optimizing algorithms and incorporating key processes.
