articles.title: High-resolution karst spring discharge datasets of the Euro-Mediterranean mountain regions
articles.titleEn: High-resolution karst spring discharge datasets of the Euro-Mediterranean mountain regions
articles.abstract: Karst groundwater systems exhibit heterogeneity in recharge, circulation, and discharge, occupying a unique position within groundwater systems. This complexity facilitates rapid responses via the preferential flow routes, making karst systems vulnerable to climatic and anthropogenic pressures. High-altitude karst aquifers are particularly susceptible to shifting climate patterns – specifically rising temperatures, declining snow cover, and increasingly less and inconsistent precipitation – within the Mediterranean climate hotspot. Effective sustainable management of these groundwater systems require robust hydrological modelling; however, the application of such models is often constrained by the availability of high-quality, reliable datasets. This study presents a comprehensive collection of high-resolution karst spring discharge data from major Euro-Mediterranean mountain belts, including the Atlas, Betics, Pyrenees, Jura, Alps, Carpathians, Apennines, Dinarides, Hellenides, Balkans, Taurus, Levant, and Zagros. We compiled a total of 129 discharge time series specifically curated for hydrological modelling. Geographically, the dataset is led by the Alps (approx. 38.7 %), followed by the Carpathians (11.7 %) and Dinarides (approx. 8.5 %), the Apennines, and Zagros each contributing approx. 6.2 %. The Levant, Pyrenees and Taurus account for approx. 5 % each, while the remaining regions (Atlas, Balkans, Betics, Hellenides, and Jura) represent less than 5 % each. In terms of temporal resolution, 92 % of the records are daily, while hourly and monthly data each comprise 4 %. The average record length is 21 years, which is led by a 98-year series from Unica Spring, Slovenia (1926–2024). Regional analysis indicates that the Jura, Balkans and Pyrenees maintain average record length exceeding 30 years of daily data, followed by the Alps, Apennines, Betics, Carpathians, and Dinarides, exceeding 20 years, whereas the Atlas, Levant, Taurus, and Zagros range between 10 and 20 years. The shortest average records were observed in the Hellenides (8 years), which is still adequate for hydrological modelling applications. The dataset can be accessed at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19448790 (Çallı et al., 2026).

articles.title: A spatially explicit dataset of agriculture liming across the contiguous United States
articles.titleEn: A spatially explicit dataset of agriculture liming across the contiguous United States
articles.abstract: Agricultural lime has historically been applied to croplands in the United States to counteract soil acidification and enhance soil fertility, with important consequences for crop productivity and Earth's carbon cycle. Previous works on agricultural liming have largely focused on either region-specific case studies or national-level estimates of total application rates, leaving a major gap in understanding the spatial variability in lime application. This study addresses this gap by presenting the first spatially explicit dataset of agricultural lime application across the contiguous United States (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15758274, Tsao et al., 2026). The dataset comprises state-level data for 1930–1950 and a more detailed county-level dataset for 1954–1987, enabling comprehensive spatial-temporal analyses at multiple scales. Counties in the Midwest region exhibited the highest total amounts of lime applied in the latter half of the twentieth century, reflecting intensive agricultural activity. These counties were characterized by higher overall lime application rates (amount of lime applied per unit of limed area each year) but relatively lower lime-treated fraction (ratio of limed area to total cropland area each year). In contrast, counties in the southeastern coastal region exhibited lower lime application rates per unit of limed area but with a higher lime-treated fraction within the agricultural areas. We used a machine learning framework to assess if the spatial variation of lime application from our dataset can be explained by agricultural and environmental factors with known agronomic relationships. Our results show that the total amount of lime applied for each county, as well as the application rate and treated fraction, can be reasonably explained with regional climatic conditions, soil properties, and agricultural management practices (such as crop production, fertilizer use, and soil pH recommendations). Spatiotemporal integration of the data product results in a revised national estimate of total lime application, with a range of 15–25 million metric tons per year (Mt yr −1 ) between 1954–1987. This study establishes a critical observational baseline of historical agricultural lime application and highlights the need for further research into its long-term environmental impacts.

articles.title: The consistent in-situ global gridded temperature and salinity dataset, CORA OA 1960–2024
articles.titleEn: The consistent in-situ global gridded temperature and salinity dataset, CORA OA 1960–2024
articles.abstract: Gridded ocean products play a pivotal role in oceanographic and climate research, providing a framework for the cross-validation and calibration of satellite observations and in-situ data. This paper describes the latest evolution of the global gridded ocean objective analysis fields for temperature and salinity, distributed by the Copernicus Marine Service. It accounts for the update of the objective analysis first guess using monthly fields derived from the temporal interpolation of World Ocean Atlas 2023 (WOA23) decadal temperature and salinity climatologies. The new product provides monthly objective analysis fields for temperature and salinity with a 0.5° horizontal resolution and 186 vertical levels covering depths from 0 to 5500 m. The dataset is updated annually and covers the period from 1960 to December of the last complete year; the version described here covers 1960–2024. A full reprocessing is conducted every November, while an interim update covering the first six months of the current year is released each June. This product was compared with other reference 3D temperature and salinity datasets, as well as SST and SSS products. It exhibits strong consistency with all reference data, particularly over the 1985–2024 period. Notably, the effects of the Argo “fast salty drift”, detected in other datasets after 2016, are limited in this product. The gridded product is freely available from the Copernicus Marine Service at https://doi.org/10.48670/mds-00383 (E.U. Copernicus Marine Service Information (CMEMS), 2026) (product ID INSITU_GLO_PHY_TS_OA_MY_013_052).

articles.title: Effects of enhanced rock weathering on soil gas fluxes across UK land uses
articles.titleEn: Effects of enhanced rock weathering on soil gas fluxes across UK land uses
articles.abstract: Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) is a proposed carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) removal strategy via the application of crushed silicate rocks to accelerate the natural breakdown of silicate minerals, permanently trapping atmospheric CO 2 . Application of rock dust may alter soil properties, such as pH, with potential consequences for soil trace gases fluxes relevant to climate forcing and air quality. However, previous ERW studies have focused mainly on the principal greenhouse gases, while broader trace gas responses remain poorly constrained. This laboratory study presents measurements of nitric oxide (NO), ammonia (NH 3 ), carbon monoxide (CO), hydrogen (H 2 ) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), as well as CO 2 , methane (CH 4 ) and nitrous oxide (N 2 O), from control and ERW-treated soils collected from arable, grassland and newly planted broadleaf and conifer forest field trials in the UK. Soils were sieved, repacked and rewetted for laboratory measurements. A dynamic air-flow-through chamber system, equipped with a high-resolution multi-gas analyser and a proton-transfer-reaction mass spectrometer, was used to measure N 2 O, NO, NH 3 , CO, and VOCs between 5 and 25 °C. CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes were measured online at 20 °C using a closed-loop chamber method, and H 2 fluxes were measured by discrete sampling from static chamber headspace using gas chromatography. ERW-associated differences varied among gases and soils, with no consistent response across all incubated samples. The reported treatment differences included lower CO 2 emissions in both forest soils, greater CH 4 uptake in broadleaf forest soil, higher NO emissions in grassland soil, and changes in CO and hydrocarbon fluxes in forest soils. NH 3 and H 2 fluxes showed no statistically significant treatment responses, and no individual VOC remained significantly different after correction for multiple testing. Overall, rock dust application had limited and inconsistent impacts on trace gas fluxes across the soils examined in this study. As these measurements represent snapshots of field ERW effects under controlled laboratory conditions from manipulated soils, longer-term in-situ measurements at ERW field trials are needed to examine how these responses vary seasonally and evolve as the applied materials continued to weather. These measurements should be accompanied by in-depth soil characterisation and microbial analyses to elucidate the complex relationships between ERW treatment and trace gas fluxes. This evidence is needed to assess the full climate, air-quality and environmental implications of large-scale ERW deployment.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Post‐2100 Climate Change
articles.titleEn: A Systematic Review of Post‐2100 Climate Change
articles.abstract: Climate services seek to inform decisions about long‐term climate changes. Since the 1990s, the vast majority of climate projections have covered the period up to 2100, a horizon that is not so distant anymore. This leaves decision makers tasked with planning coastal development or building long‐lived infrastructure with relatively sparse information to assess climate risks, evaluate the costs and benefits of adaptation options, and implement carbon emission mitigation actions. In a bid to better understand how climate services could extend further into the future, this paper reviews the literature to understand how and why post‐2100 climate studies are conducted. It identifies three broad themes: understanding climate processes with great inertia, assessing climate risks and informing adaptation actions, and evaluating emission mitigation scenarios. Multiple papers reveal the complex interplay between climate feedbacks, and show how climate change post‐2100 is not merely an extension of 21st century trends. The overwhelming focus on the current century downplays the long‐term damages of current emissions and fails to convey the possibility that future climate conditions could exceed adaptation capacity. We reiterate numerous calls made in the literature to extend mainstream climate emission scenarios and climate model projections farther into the future, and provide the building blocks for robust climate products.

articles.title: Who Migrates? Social Identity and the Limits of Climate Adaptation
articles.titleEn: Who Migrates? Social Identity and the Limits of Climate Adaptation
articles.abstract: Migration is increasingly framed as a key climate adaptation strategy, yet this framing often overlooks how social hierarchies structure the feasibility of migration. We investigate this relationship in South India, a critical development context characterized by high caste stratification, out‐migration, and rainfall variability. We conceptualize migration as a threshold process in which household capacity increases the feasibility of moving, while social identity may constrain the translation of capacity into adaptive action. Using repeated cross‐sectional data from 27,122 households linked with high‐resolution rainfall data, we estimate migration responses to rainfall variability across different caste groups. We find that marginalized caste groups have substantially lower migration probabilities under normal rainfall conditions, but they become significantly more responsive as rainfall anomalies become more severe. This pattern suggests a bifurcation in adaptation behavior: while advantaged groups migrate more under typical conditions, marginalized groups are more responsive to severe rainfall stressors. Counterfactual simulations show that migration gaps persist even when household capacities are equalized. These findings suggest that adaptation inequality is not merely a problem of endowment deficits but of identity‐based constraints tied to caste, requiring policies that address the structural barriers to adaptation.

articles.title: Large Projected Increase in Cloud‐to‐Ground Lightning Under Future Climate
articles.titleEn: Large Projected Increase in Cloud‐to‐Ground Lightning Under Future Climate
articles.abstract: Cloud‐to‐ground (CG) lightning poses significant risks to infrastructure, people, and ecosystems. However, while many studies have projected changes in total lightning under warming, future trends in CG lightning remain poorly constrained. Here, we combine ground‐based CG lightning observations with six daily surface meteorological variables (mean temperature, total precipitation, short‐wave radiation, relative humidity, pressure, wind speed) to predict CG lightning density over land at 0.5° resolution using an XGBoost machine learning model. The model accurately captures contemporary spatial and temporal lightning patterns and outperforms an alternative multiple linear regression model as well as three existing parameterizations based on convective precipitation or convective available potential energy times precipitation. Applying the XGBoost model to historical climate shows a 11% increase in global CG lightning frequency over the 20th century. Future projections using outputs from two climate models (MPI‐ESM1‐2‐HR and UKESM1‐0‐LL) reveal large increases of 76%–140% under a high‐emission scenario (SSP3‐7.0), equivalent to roughly 30% more CG lightning per degree of global warming. These increases are substantially higher than those projected by the linear model and previous studies. Absolute increases are largest in the tropics, while relative increases are largest at high latitudes, where lightning density often more than doubles. The largest uncertainties emerge in the tropics for UKESM1‐0‐LL climate, particularly in the Amazon and New Guinea, where future climate differs strongly from current conditions. Our results suggest that climate change may substantially amplify CG lightning frequency, underscoring the need for improved risk assessments.

articles.title: Weather Sensitivity to Sea Surface Temperatures Over the Contiguous United States in a Medium Ensemble of High‐Resolution Regionally Refined Simulations Using E3SM
articles.titleEn: Weather Sensitivity to Sea Surface Temperatures Over the Contiguous United States in a Medium Ensemble of High‐Resolution Regionally Refined Simulations Using E3SM
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Climate model simulations have long been invaluable tools for synoptic meteorology. However, they are generally too coarse in resolution to resolve fine‐scale extreme weather, which require stronger spatial gradients and sharper representations of topography. Here we perform an ensemble of sea surface temperature (SST)‐forced experiments with the Energy Exascale Earth System Model, applying its regionally‐refined model capability over the contiguous United States. The prescribed SSTs are historically‐derived and designed to represent recurrent patterns of Pacific Ocean variability. Our ensemble allows for understanding of how leading modes of ocean variability affect global hydroclimate but with the added capacity to resolve extreme weather at regional scale over the US. We focus our study on how ocean modes of variability specifically affect extreme heat and extreme precipitation events, snowpack, tropical cyclones, and atmospheric rivers. We find that extreme weather is realistically simulated at regional scale but shown to have a persistent wet precipitation bias and warm temperature bias, which impacts the utility of the ensemble. Nonetheless, our simulations provide a large sample of highly impactful extremes, including extremes possible over the historical period but without a historical analog, and their response to ocean variability.

articles.title: Porous Cavities and Smooth Boundaries: Brinkman Volume Penalization for Ice‐Shelf–Ocean Interactions in Ocean General Circulation Models
articles.titleEn: Porous Cavities and Smooth Boundaries: Brinkman Volume Penalization for Ice‐Shelf–Ocean Interactions in Ocean General Circulation Models
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Numerical ocean models remain essential for investigating ice–shelf–ocean interaction to estimate the fate of the Antarctic Ice Sheet in a warming climate. A persistent challenge in ‐coordinate ocean models is the artificial stepwise representation of cavity geometries, which induces excessive diapycnal mixing and numerical noise beneath the ice draft. Here, we assess the potential of the Brinkman Volume Penalization (BVP) method for ice–ocean modeling, in which the ice–ocean interface is replaced by a porous region that is partially ocean and partially ice. The benefits of penalization are evaluated in a ‐coordinate ocean model using an idealized ISOMIP+ configuration (Asay‐Davis et al., 2016, https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd‐9‐2471‐2016 ) under both warm and cold scenarios. First, smoothing the cavity with the BVP acts as an effective local increase in vertical resolution, improving ocean circulation near the grounding line and allowing strong basal melt at the ice‐shelf base. Second, we show that the distribution of heat and meltwater within the penalized region reduces spurious mixing, leading to colder and fresher ice‐shelf waters and a strengthened overturning circulation. Hence, the BVP approach provides a promising alternative to a Losch (2008, https://doi.org/10.1029/2007jc004368 ) melt‐layer formulation, for which similar noise reduction requires prescribing a melt‐layer depth that is too large and leads to excessive mixing. Finally, we show that at least four vertical grid cells are required to resolve grounding‐zone overturning and to obtain strong and consistent basal melt patterns. In summary, these results provide practical guidance for improving the numerical treatment of ice‐shelf cavities in OGCMs.

articles.title: Last glacial North Pacific oxygenation due to North Atlantic circulation changes
articles.titleEn: Last glacial North Pacific oxygenation due to North Atlantic circulation changes
articles.abstract: Oxygen minimum zones, subsurface regions of the ocean severely depleted in dissolved oxygen, today extend over more than 30 million km 2 . Although these areas are expected to expand in the future in response to warming, the magnitude of deoxygenation is poorly constrained. Here we present a quantitative spatio-temporal reconstruction of oxygen minimum zone changes in the subarctic and eastern North Pacific over the last 55 thousand years based on 2,569 individual foraminiferal assemblage measurements from 11 sedimentary cores. We find that the extent of oxygen minimum zones in the eastern North Pacific expanded in response to warming during Dansgaard–Oeschger events during the last glacial period and through the last deglaciation. However, re-oxygenation events and oxygen minimum zone contraction also occurred in the last glacial period when overturning circulation weakened in the North Atlantic during Heinrich events. Our findings, supported by Earth system simulations confirming a strong coupling between millennial-scale changes in North Atlantic circulation and North Pacific oxygen minimum zone extent, imply a complex future response of the oxygen minimum zone extent, with global circulation changes potentially mitigating the direct effects of warming.

articles.title: New insights from fully-integrated surface-subsurface hydrological modeling in high-elevation glaciated environments
articles.titleEn: New insights from fully-integrated surface-subsurface hydrological modeling in high-elevation glaciated environments
articles.abstract: Recent modeling efforts go towards distributed physics-based modeling for improved hydrological process understanding. The sparse hydro-meteorological observations and complex topography in high-elevation mountainous environments have, however, hampered the application of such data-intensive and sophisticated techniques for detailed process exploration. In particular, characterizing surface-subsurface water exchange processes in these terrains remains understudied. Here we implement a fully-integrated and fully-distributed surface-subsurface hydrological model, WaSiM , to quantify the observed daily streamflow variations and their interactions with groundwater in the high-elevation glaciated catchment (Martell Valley) in the central European Alps since the 2000s. Extensive field observations (meteorology, vegetation, glacier mass balance, soil properties, river discharge), especially in-situ groundwater levels, were collected to investigate hydrological processes and constrain model parameters in the surface and subsurface. We observe that in contrast to the delayed responses typically observed in aquifers, shallow alpine groundwater responds nearly as quickly as streamflow to peak snowmelt and extreme rainfall events, highlighting the need for improved subsurface parametrization in hydrological modeling. Joint evaluation against shallow groundwater heads and streamflow shows that the daily streamflow and shallow groundwater dynamics can be reproduced without requiring the WaSiM interflow component, providing new constraints on the representation of unsaturated-zone flow pathways in high Alpine hydrological models. Moreover, to improve the integration of point-scale groundwater observations into fully-distributed models, we suggest pre-calculating the Topographic Wetness Index to stratify hydro-topographic settings and combining this information with other site characteristics to guide piezometer placement. Despite uncertainties associated with model structure and subsurface representation, this study demonstrates the value of groundwater observations for constraining internal flow partitioning in hydrological modeling.

articles.title: Present and future responses of near-surface wind speed to different land-use and land-cover types in China
articles.titleEn: Present and future responses of near-surface wind speed to different land-use and land-cover types in China
articles.abstract: Near-surface wind speed (NSWS) is highly sensitive to land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). However, previous studies have mainly focused on overall LULCC effects, leaving the attribution of wind variations to individual land transitions and management poorly constrained. Here, we utilize simulations from the latest Land-Use Model Intercomparison Project to disentangle and quantify the responses of NSWS to different types of LULCC over China from 1970 to 2014. We demonstrate that the primary-to-grazing transition is the dominant factor contributing to LULCC-induced NSWS variability, followed by fertilizer use, while urbanization makes the smallest contribution among the examined LULCC types. Future projections further suggest that land-use pathways can substantially perturb wind patterns, with low-emission pathways combined with minimally regulated land use producing more pronounced alterations than high-emission pathways combined with sustainable land use. These results highlight the importance of resolving LULCC in attributing and projecting NSWS changes, with implications for climate modeling, wind-energy assessment, and land-use policy.

articles.title: Historical Nansen cast temperature profiles and the ocean heat content changes since 19th century
articles.titleEn: Historical Nansen cast temperature profiles and the ocean heat content changes since 19th century
articles.abstract: Ocean heat content (OHC) estimates rely on subsurface temperature observations whose abundance, quality, and accuracy have changed over time as oceanographic techniques and methods have developed. The majority of the available global OHC time series begins in the 1950s when the International Geophysical Year 1957-1958 (IGY) observational campaign resulted in a rapid improvement of the observational basis. However, a significant amount of subsurface temperature observations had already been accumulated before the IGY. Extending knowledge back in time beyond current estimates provides further insight into global changes in the ocean-atmosphere system. We perform a three-step quality control (QC) of the Nansen cast temperature profiles with a focus on the time period before 1970. The QC includes automated and manual control of temperature observations, along with the quality control of temperature anomalies. We use the World Ocean Circulation Experiment/Argo Global Hydrographic climatology, based on high-quality temperature observations between 1990 and 2025, as the reference. To interpolate temperatures vertically, we use the temperature anomaly method by Frankignoul (1981). This method yields smaller interpolation errors than linear interpolation and the Reiniger and Ross (1968) parabolic method. Corrections for depth bias in Nansen cast profiles are also suggested. The oldest temperature profiles from the 1870s are treated separately, with the data from the “Challenger” expedition used as reference. Finally, we estimate the OHC changes between the 1870s and the 2020s for six selected multi-year time periods. We find that for the layer 0–2000 m the OHC increase between 1920–1944 and 1945–1969 amounts to 32.7±6.8/37.5±3.8 % of the total OHC increase between 1920–1944 and 2010–2025 for original and depth corrected profiles respectively. The complete dataset is freely available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22764102 (Gouretski et al., 2026a) and https://doi.org/10.12157/IOCAS.20260520.001 (Gouretski et al., 2026b).

articles.title: Dataset of a 4 km combined seismic and electric streamer survey along the embankment of the Po river in Crescentino
articles.titleEn: Dataset of a 4 km combined seismic and electric streamer survey along the embankment of the Po river in Crescentino
articles.abstract: For river embankment characterization non-invasive geophysical investigations are a valuable complementary tool to standard geotechnical testing. To this aim, resistivity and seismic methods can be complementary to each other, providing information about pore fluid properties and solid skeleton characteristics, respectively. The use of streamer cables for these surveys can reduce the acquisition time, making geophysical investigations ideal as a preliminary screening tool for the identification of localized anomalies. Few examples of combined seismic and electric streamer systems were already proposed in the literature, but their applicability for long and extensive surveys still needs to be showcased. Moreover, tailored processing methods are necessary given the large amount of data collected with the above mentioned acquisition systems, which can be challenging for standard processing and inversion software and require calibration of devoted interpretation techniques. We present a dataset of a 4 km combined seismic and electric streamer survey acquired along the embankment of the Po River in Crescentino, near Torino, in north-west Italy. Data acquisition strategies are discussed and preliminary data analyses are reported. The survey demonstrated the efficiency and potentiality of combined seismic and electric streamer systems in investigating river embankments. All the acquired geophysical data, together with complementary geotechnical, topographic and meteorological information, are made available in a structured dataset (Vergnano et al., 2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18183049). The presented dataset can be an ideal playground to test and benchmark alternative processing and interpretation approaches, and enable an advancement in the state-of-the-art of these characterization methodologies.

articles.title: A global 3D chlorophyll a dataset derived from multimodal deep learning reconstruction
articles.titleEn: A global 3D chlorophyll a dataset derived from multimodal deep learning reconstruction
articles.abstract: Chlorophyll a (Chl a ) is a key variable for characterizing marine phytoplankton biomass and upper-ocean biogeochemical variability. Existing global products are generally limited to the ocean surface and therefore cannot adequately resolve subsurface vertical structure. In this study, a multimodal Profile-Surface Transformer (PST) framework was developed by integrating Biogeochemical-Argo (BGC-Argo) Chl a profiles, Core-Argo temperature-salinity profiles, and satellite-derived surface Chl a to reconstruct the three-dimensional (3D) vertical structure of Chl a from 10 to 500 m depth. A global monthly mean 3D Chl a dataset at 1° spatial resolution for January 2005–June 2025 was subsequently constructed. Evaluation of the dataset demonstrates that PST exhibits robust stability and effective profile reconstruction capability across various generalization scenarios. The coefficients of determination under random split, year-based split, and spatial cross-validation are 0.89, 0.87, and 0.86 ± 0.01, respectively. Furthermore, independent external validation using ship-based observations confirms that the model maintains good generalization performance across different observing systems. The constructed dataset successfully reproduces known global patterns of Chl a vertical structure and its subsurface chlorophyll maximum (SCM), as well as their seasonal variability. Variability in SCM depth is primarily characterized by regionally heterogeneous redistribution superimposed on a persistent zonal background, rather than by a pronounced monotonic change in the global mean depth. Overall, the constructed long-term 3D Chl a dataset integrates surface observations and discrete biogeochemical profiles, delivering a new observationally constrained global product. This dataset is well-suited for studies on the vertical ecological structure of phytoplankton, long-term ocean biogeochemical variability, and the responses of upper-ocean ecosystems to climate change. The dataset is publicly available from Zenodo (Meng et al., 2026a) at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22726410.

articles.title: Land Abandonment and Climate Warming Drove Two Centuries of Natural Forest Expansion in the Alps
articles.titleEn: Land Abandonment and Climate Warming Drove Two Centuries of Natural Forest Expansion in the Alps
articles.abstract: Natural forest expansion (NFE) is a widespread consequence of land abandonment and climate change in mountain systems, yet its long‐term spatiotemporal patterns and the relative influence of land‐use and climate change remain poorly resolved. Here we compile and analyse a harmonized dataset of forest cover derived from historical maps and aerial/satellite imagery to assess NFE across the European Alps over the past 200 years. Using machine learning and spatial statistical models, we quantified spatiotemporal changes and analysed the trade‐offs between drivers of NFE over time. NFE in the region was quantified in 1.55 million ha since the early 19th century (16% of the European Alps), with a peak between the end of World War II and the 1980s (11,260 ha year −1 ), largely driven by widespread land abandonment. Although conservation efforts intensified during this period, protected areas were typically designated in high‐elevation and remote areas already undergoing forest transitions, suggesting they followed rather than initiated change. Over the last four decades, the pace of NFE has slowed (7195 ha year −1 ), spatial clustering has weakened, and forest gains have increasingly shifted toward treeline ecotones. Together, our results indicate a system in transition, with a temporal reorganization of forest expansion from land‐use legacies and gap filling toward stronger environmental constraints at higher elevations. These findings provide a long‐term perspective on how interacting socio‐economic and climatic drivers shape forest transitions in mountain regions under ongoing global change.

articles.title: Unveiling carbonate dissolution in coastal sediments and its influence on seawater buffering capacity with δ 13 C DIC and 224 Ra– 228 Th disequilibria
articles.titleEn: Unveiling carbonate dissolution in coastal sediments and its influence on seawater buffering capacity with δ 13 C DIC and 224 Ra– 228 Th disequilibria
articles.abstract: Organic carbon mineralization is generally recognized as the primary source of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) released from sediments in coastal seas. The CO 2 accumulation or the formation of corrosive microenvironment induced by organic carbon degradation can promote the dissolution of calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) in sediments, complicating the efficiency of carbon burial and total alkalinity (TA) inputs to aquatic environments. However, quantitative assessments of sediment CaCO 3 dissolution and its impacts on the seawater carbonate remain poorly constrained. In this study, we selected typical high-productivity regions, mariculture farms, and applied the 224 Ra– 228 Th disequilibrium approach to quantify the effluxes of DIC and TA across the sediment-water interface. The stable carbon isotope of DIC ( δ 13 C DIC ) was employed to trace DIC sources in porewater. The results showed that CaCO 3 dissolution in the sediment accounted for 29±13 % to 55±10 % of the benthic DIC effluxes. Notably, a high contribution of CaCO 3 dissolution did not coincide with strong organic carbon degradation across sites, suggesting that dynamic disturbance in the sediment, which weakened the metabolic CO 2 accumulation in porewater, was also a crucial factor affecting carbonate dissolution. According to the evaluation of the influence that benthic DIC and TA effluxes exerted on the seawater CO 2 content, the TA supplied by the CaCO 3 dissolution was identified to enhance the carbonate buffering capacity of seawater and counteracted the acidification driven by organic matter remineralization. This indicates that CaCO 3 dissolution in sediments should be involved in coastal carbon cycling and assessments on coastal ecosystem resilience under the risk of CO 2 elevation.

articles.title: Forecasting the flame: simulating future wildfire regimes in the Northeast Mediterranean
articles.titleEn: Forecasting the flame: simulating future wildfire regimes in the Northeast Mediterranean
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Despite a global decline in total burned area, high-impact wildfire events continue to pose growing threats to ecosystems and human communities. As climate change amplifies hydroclimatic extremes, cycles of precipitation-driven fuel build-up followed by persistent drought are increasing the likelihood of severe wildfires. Moving beyond estimates of total burned area, this study aims to answer “where, and how often, will future landscapes burn?” by quantifying wildfire hazard through fire probability and fire return intervals for the northern segment of the Eastern Mediterranean Basin (34–46° N, 24–50° E), a region where such extremes are expected to fundamentally alter fire regimes. Potential changes in fire activity were investigated for the period 1961–2100 using the process-based dynamic vegetation model LPJ-GUESS coupled with SIMFIRE–BLAZE wildfire modules. Terrestrial vegetation was represented using regionally parameterised Plant Functional Types, and simulations were forced with ERA5-Land reanalysis for the historical period (1961–2025) and an ensemble of five CMIP6 climate projections under a high-emissions scenario (SSP5-8.5) for exploratory future analysis (2015–2100). Benchmarking against MODIS MCD64A1 observations revealed that while the model successfully reproduced domain-scale burned area magnitudes and interannual variability, weak spatial agreement highlighted the strong influence of localised anthropogenic ignition and suppression processes not represented in the natural-potential experimental design. Future projections indicated that changes in fire probability and return intervals are unlikely to be spatially uniform. Instead, simulation results highlight a fundamental reorganization of fire regimes driven by the interplay between hydroclimatic change, vegetation dynamics, and landscape structure. By combining temporally explicit reanalysis data with ensemble climate projections, this study distinguishes between the role of observed hydroclimatic extremes in shaping historical fire activity and the importance of long-term climate trajectories in constraining future risk. The findings suggest that climate change may not simply increase overall wildfire activity in the Northeast Mediterranean, but rather systematically redistribute fire risk across its distinct ecoregions, with urgent implications for anticipating emerging hotspots and adapting fire management strategies.

articles.title: Characterizing orographic clouds and precipitation in Qilian Mountains, northwestern China
articles.titleEn: Characterizing orographic clouds and precipitation in Qilian Mountains, northwestern China
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Orographic precipitation plays a critical role in water resource and hydrologic cycle in many arid and semiarid regions of the world. The formation and characteristics for an orographic precipitation event on 16–17 August 2020 (Beijing Time, UTC+8) in Qilian Mountains of northwestern China are investigated based on observational data and high-resolution (up to 333 m) simulations of Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model. The results show that the local mountain-valley wind circulation plays a critical role in the formation of orographic clouds and precipitation, showing an obvious daily variation. In the afternoon, due to strong solar radiation heating, there is an obvious upslope wind on the sunny side of the mountain, the airflow on the windward slope was blocked and lifted, a strong terrain wave was excited, resulting in strong convective clouds and precipitation. In the evening, due to the strong long-wave radiation cooling effect of the mountains, the strong downslope wind generated converges and lifts at the valley bottom, which promotes the development of weak convective and stratiform clouds over the valley. In the early hours of the morning, the downslope wind reaches its strongest level, producing a strong downhill wind circulation (mountain wind), and a strong uplift effect at the bottom of the valley, forming a deep layered cloud and precipitation process. In the afternoon, the convective clouds are dominant. The microphysical process is mainly characterized by high content of graupel particles. The sources of rainwater are mainly from the warm rain process via collision-coalescence and the melting process of graupel particles, accounting for 30.3 % and 23.6 % respectively. In the evening and early morning, weak convective and stratiform clouds are dominant. The melting of snow is the main source of rainwater, accounting for 92.6 %; The precipitation conversion rate is basically consistent with the temporal evolution of precipitation over time, and with the increase of terrain height, the precipitation conversion rate in this area also increases. These quantitative findings provide a physical basis for improving microphysical parameterization schemes and guiding cloud-seeding operations, bearing important implications for water resource management in the Qilian Mountains and analogous semi-arid mountainous regions worldwide.

articles.title: Forecast‐Informed Industrial Scheduling for Air Quality, Health, and Equity Cobenefits in Developing Asia
articles.titleEn: Forecast‐Informed Industrial Scheduling for Air Quality, Health, and Equity Cobenefits in Developing Asia
articles.abstract: Air pollution stemming from fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) remains a major public health challenge across China, India, and Southeast Asia, especially during severe pollution episodes. Existing management strategies often rely on long‐term structural reforms or short‐term emergency controls, both of which can involve notable economic costs and social disruption. Here, we examined whether seasonal PM 2.5 forecasts could help inform anticipatory industrial scheduling as a complementary approach to pollution mitigation. Using an integrated prediction‐to‐policy framework in which seasonal climate forecasts, atmospheric chemical transport modeling, and high‐resolution exposure assessment are combined, we evaluated this concept within the policy context of the emission control measures implemented during the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics and explored its broader regional implications through stylized scenario analysis. Under the modeled conditions, forecast‐informed scheduling was associated with reductions in PM 2.5 concentrations ranging from 5% to 30%. From October 2021 to February 2022, the intervention scenario was associated with an estimated 12.2% decrease in PM 2.5 ‐attributable short‐term premature mortality, corresponding to 66,900 avoided deaths (95% confidence interval (CI): 46,990–86,912), and health‐related economic savings of US$84.4 billion, which is equivalent to approximately 0.18% of the regional gross domestic product. The benefits were relatively balanced across income groups in China but were typically greater for lower‐income populations in India and Southeast Asia during high‐pollution episodes. These findings provide a regional proof of concept that seasonal environmental prediction may help inform earlier and more targeted air quality management in developing Asia, while the magnitude of the modeled benefits depends on the scenario assumptions and local implementation conditions.

articles.title: Characterizing runoff response to rainfall in permafrost catchments and its implications for hydrological and biogeochemical fluxes in a warming climate
articles.titleEn: Characterizing runoff response to rainfall in permafrost catchments and its implications for hydrological and biogeochemical fluxes in a warming climate
articles.abstract: Understanding how Arctic catchments respond to rainfall is critical for anticipating hydrological and biogeochemical effects of a warming climate. We use ensemble rainfall-runoff analysis (ERRA) to identify how runoff response to rainfall varies with meteorological, subsurface, and geomorphic conditions across three permafrost catchments: Upper Kuparuk (Alaska) and the Goose and Ptarmigan catchments (Cape Bounty, Nunavut, Canadian High Arctic). ERRA enables us to quantify event-scale runoff responses to rainfall using high-resolution, multi-year hydrometeorological datasets, and test how variations in rainfall intensity, thaw depth, antecedent effective wetness, and active layer detachments (ALDs) affect runoff behavior. At Upper Kuparuk, our results show that peak runoff response increases by more than five-fold in response to increases in antecedent streamflow (a proxy for antecedent effective wetness), and is also higher in summers with higher average precipitation. By contrast, at the same catchment, warmer winters and springs are associated with reduced runoff sensitivity to rainfall. Furthermore, a paired watershed comparison shows that streamflow and riverine fluxes of dissolved solids, suspended sediment, and particulate organic carbon are more readily mobilized by rainfall inputs when ALDs are present. Considered together, these findings highlight the difficulty in generalizing climate-driven runoff trends in permafrost regions subject to competing and interacting controls, such as precipitation intensity, storage capacity and permafrost stability. Our findings offer a more nuanced alternative to broad classifications of Arctic landscapes as “drying” or “wetting” under climate change.

articles.title: Contrasting Fire‐Driven Erosion Processes Mobilise Distinct Organic Carbon Pools in Forest Landscapes
articles.titleEn: Contrasting Fire‐Driven Erosion Processes Mobilise Distinct Organic Carbon Pools in Forest Landscapes
articles.abstract: Wildfires can substantially alter organic carbon (C) cycling in forest ecosystems beyond immediate emissions from fuel combustion. Among these post‐fire effects, lateral C mobilisation by water erosion is an important but poorly quantified flux, rarely incorporated into fire‐related C budgets. Here, we quantified and characterised C mobilised by hillslope erosion and channel erosion by debris flows in highly fire‐prone eucalypt forests in southeastern Australia. We monitored suspended and bedload C export from headwater catchments across fire severities until erosion returned to background levels, quantified C mobilisation from colluvium by debris flows, characterised C chemical recalcitrance in ash, soils, eroded sediments and colluvium, and constrained colluvial C age using radiocarbon measurements. We then upscaled these fluxes to the area affected by the 2009 Beechworth Fire. Over the three‐year post‐fire perturbation period, hillslope and channel erosion mobilised 15,866 t C (0.78 t C ha −1 ). Hillslope erosion accounted for 91% of this landscape‐scale flux, compared with 9% from debris flows. The two processes mobilised contrasting C pools. Hillslope C export was dominated by young wildfire ash derived from incompletely combusted vegetation and the surface organic soil horizon. In contrast, debris flows generated substantial localised C pulses by eroding deeper colluvial deposits, with 2%–20% of mobilised C older than 6000 years. Chemically recalcitrant and highly recalcitrant forms accounted for 47%–60% of C in fire‐affected hillslope sediments and 43%–74% in colluvium, highlighting the potential importance of these lateral fluxes for long‐term C dynamics. Post‐fire erosion mobilised C equivalent to only approximately 4% of direct fire C emissions, but the C mobilised during the three‐year post‐fire period was equivalent to approximately 210 years of background (unburnt) erosion. Thus, lateral erosion represents an additional and compositionally distinct pathway of fire‐driven C redistribution that should be considered in fire‐prone forest C budgets.

articles.title: Building a random forest machine learning model for annual Net Ecosystem Exchange estimation in agricultural fields using discontinuous atmospheric Eddy Covariance measurements
articles.titleEn: Building a random forest machine learning model for annual Net Ecosystem Exchange estimation in agricultural fields using discontinuous atmospheric Eddy Covariance measurements
articles.abstract: Atmospheric CO 2 exchanges in agroecosystems are strongly controlled by plant phenology, management and microclimatic conditions; yet obtaining finely resolved flux estimates across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes remains challenging. This study evaluates the ability of a single Eddy Covariance (EC) system combined with wind-sector partitioning and Random Forest (RF) modelling to estimate the annual Net Ecosystem Exchange (NEE) of adjacent fields (wheat, mixed-grain, permanent grassland) in the Marais poitevin wetland (French Atlantic coast). Fluxes were measured over the period 1 February 2023–31 January 2024 and attributed to eight wind sectors, each used as a proxy for the corresponding field or landscape feature that dominates its footprint. Two modelling strategies were compared (i) a single global RF trained on all sectors and (ii) sector-specific RFs trained separately for each wind sector. RF models globally showed good overall performance ( R 2 ≈0.20–0.94 depending on sector and period), but this apparent equivalence broke down once fluxes were reconstructed over the full annual cycle: the sector-specific approach then better reproduced phenological dynamics and management-driven flux reversals (harvest, senescence) than the global model, which compressed inter-sector variability by up to 70 %. Annual NEE estimated from the sector-specific models indicated that the mixed-grain field acted as net source (+151 g C m −2 yr −1 ), whereas the permanent grassland and the wheat field acted as net sinks (−145 and −308 g C m −2 yr −1 , respectively). A light-response-curve partitioning of these reconstructed fluxes into gross primary production (GPP) and ecosystem respiration (Reco) revealed contrasting phenological signatures behind different land-covers. Methodology and associated limitations/uncertainties due to flux measurement and modelling, footprint attribution and sector delineation, and the limited one-year observation period are particularly addressed. This study highlights the novelty and practical value of coupling a single EC system with wind-sector partitioning and machine learning approaches to resolve carbon fluxes at the field scale within heterogeneous agricultural landscapes. This integrated approach provides an alternative to traditional multi-tower setups, offering new opportunities to monitor spatial carbon dynamics and management effects in real agricultural mosaics. Beyond methodological innovation, this work provides one of the first field-scale, uncertainty-resolved carbon flux datasets for a mosaic of contrasting agricultural land covers monitored by a single EC tower, offering a transferable framework to better constrain the terrestrial carbon balance of retro-littoral wet and agricultural landscapes.

articles.title: Evaluating GNSS-T VOD sensitivity to plant water dynamics, rainfall interception, and dew in a coniferous forest
articles.titleEn: Evaluating GNSS-T VOD sensitivity to plant water dynamics, rainfall interception, and dew in a coniferous forest
articles.abstract: Monitoring forest canopy water is essential for understanding drought response and interception losses under climate change. At short timescales, canopy water is partitioned among internal plant water storage ( S p ), rainfall interception ( S i ), and dew ( S d ), which together regulate plant functioning, canopy evaporation, and precipitation partitioning, yet are rarely observed simultaneously. GNSS transmissometry (GNSS-T) has recently emerged as a low-cost, continuous, stand-scale method to observe L-band vegetation optical depth (VOD) from signal attenuation. However, interpreting GNSS-T VOD remains difficult because the signal integrates multiple water pools and is similarly affected by biomass, canopy structure, and measurement noise. Here, we applied GNSS-T in a mature Picea abies stand in Tharandt, Germany, during the 2024 growing season to separate canopy water storage into S i , S d , and S p . Rainfall interception was simulated with the multilayer Penman-Rutter model CanWat and used to calibrate the empirical VOD to water storage relationship and to convert the GNSS-T noise floor into an equivalent storage detectability threshold. GNSS-T VOD tracked interception storage robustly and approximately linearly at both 30 min and event scales (R2=0.63/0.81), and modeled S i explained VOD variability better than gross precipitation alone. The inferred attenuation coefficient b was comparable in magnitude to reported L-band values and showed a seasonal variation, which we accounted for with monthly binned calibrations of b . Dew-related wetting signals were distinguishable in VOD and yielded plausible mean nightly amounts, while the largest predictions exceeded reported values and physical boundaries, which we attribute to residual noise in the VOD data. Diurnal changes in internal plant water storage were not directly detectable at sub-daily and daily scales, indicating that variations in S p remained below the GNSS-T noise floor during the study period, as shown with trait-based estimates of maximum plant water loss. This storage-versus-noise framework provides a practical way to benchmark the hydraulic sensitivity of GNSS-T across sites that differ in biomass, hydraulic strategy, and climate, and further highlights noise reduction as a prerequisite for plant-hydraulic applications. This study further promotes GNSS-T VOD as a robust monitoring instrument for resolving sub-event interception storage, a potential avenue for constraining hydrological models.

articles.title: Climate warming-induced agricultural nitrous oxide emissions can offset mitigation benefits of fertiliser reduction
articles.titleEn: Climate warming-induced agricultural nitrous oxide emissions can offset mitigation benefits of fertiliser reduction
articles.abstract: Agriculture is the dominant source of anthropogenic nitrous oxide (N 2 O), a potent greenhouse gas with a high global warming potential. In Switzerland, substantial changes in fertiliser use alongside climatic conditions have occurred over the past four decades, yet the relative contributions of management practices versus environmental change to long-term N 2 O emission trends remain incompletely understood. Here, we applied the biogeochemical model DayCent at 1 km resolution across Switzerland, integrating spatially explicit datasets on climate, soil properties and agricultural management, to quantify N 2 O emissions for the period 1981–2020 from croplands and grasslands and attribute emission changes to management versus climate drivers. Simulated national N 2 O emissions from agricultural soils declined by roughly 5 % from 4.0 to 3.8 kt N yr −1 between the 1980s and 2010s, primarily due to a 25 % reduction in N fertiliser use. Our attribution simulations suggested that under real climate conditions, such a decrease in fertiliser N inputs (−25 %) over the period studied lowered emissions by 15.2 % in croplands and by 12.0 % in grasslands (including permanent meadows and pastures, and high alpine summer pastures). articles.title: Assessing Regional Projections of Marine Climatic Impact‐Drivers Using Coordinated Ensembles: Framework and Application to the Mediterranean Sea
articles.titleEn: Assessing Regional Projections of Marine Climatic Impact‐Drivers Using Coordinated Ensembles: Framework and Application to the Mediterranean Sea
articles.abstract: The Mediterranean Sea is among the most climate‐sensitive regions globally, having experienced unprecedented sea surface temperatures, intensified marine heatwaves, and associated ecosystem impacts in recent years. These changes are projected to intensify throughout the 21st century, with implications for marine ecosystems, biogeochemical processes, and coastal societies. Here, we provide a transferable framework for assessing marine climatic impact‐drivers (CIDs) based on key physical ocean essential climate variables, integrating model evaluation, simulation filtering, and confidence assessment of projected changes across global warming levels. The framework is applied to the Mediterranean Sea using a coordinated ensemble of 29 multi‐decadal simulations from high‐resolution regional climate system models participating in Med‐CORDEX. A novel set of marine CIDs is assessed across warming levels from 1.5°C to 4°C, encompassing mean and extreme ocean temperature, mean ocean salinity, vertical stratification, and wind‐driven ocean dynamics at basin, sub‐basin, and coastal scales. Overall, model responses broadly align with historical trends, increasing confidence in projected changes. Projections indicate robust increases in mean ocean temperature, warm extremes, and stratification across regions as warming intensifies. Under high warming levels, extreme warm events become near‐yearly occurrences, whereas cold spells virtually disappear. In contrast, projected changes in salinity, wind stress extremes, and coastal upwelling remain comparatively uncertain across most regions. Beyond the Mediterranean, the proposed framework provides a consistent basis for assessing marine climate risks in other regions as high‐resolution regional projections become available, while remaining adaptable to new indicators. To facilitate the exploration of Mediterranean CID projections, an interactive web tool is provided.

articles.title: Advancing Sub‐Surface Hydrology Through WRF‐Hydro/MODFLOW Coupling: Interface Structure and Showcase Demonstration
articles.titleEn: Advancing Sub‐Surface Hydrology Through WRF‐Hydro/MODFLOW Coupling: Interface Structure and Showcase Demonstration
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Conventional land surface models (LSMs) have evolved to represent detailed physics for many aspects of water flow and transport but still suffer from missing/simplified processes at the (lower) subsurface boundary. These gaps limit ability to simulate sub‐surface and surface water and energy fluxes. We present a dynamic framework for coupling of the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) MODFLOW, an open‐source hydrologic model representing subsurface hydrology, to WRF‐Hydro, a predominantly surface‐water‐focused hydrologic modeling system. The Basic Model Interface (BMI) coupling standard is used to communicate information between the hydrologic process components of WRF‐Hydro (i.e., the Noah‐Multiparameterization (Noah‐MP) and surface routing modules) and the MODFLOW groundwater component. The BMI functions initialize WRF‐Hydro and MODFLOW simulations, update model states and fluxes (passing groundwater recharge and discharge between WRF‐Hydro and MODFLOW), and finalize the run. The USGS National Groundwater Model, a calibrated steady‐state MODFLOW model, is used as the baseline groundwater model in simulations. The new coupled WRF‐Hydro/MODFLOW model is tested over the Republican and Delaware River basins, contrasting test beds with different climates and surface water‐groundwater coupling and complexities. The dynamics of the coupled framework are assessed through tracking changes in hydrologic processes. Two‐way WRF‐Hydro/MODFLOW coupling increased deep‐soil moisture retention and surface evapotranspiration, particularly in low‐relief areas. Groundwater dynamics were largely controlled by transient recharge from WRF‐Hydro highlighting the value of integrated modeling for capturing spatiotemporal hydrologic variability. This modeling effort seeks to advance the representation of groundwater in land and hydrological models and to improve the quantification of groundwater‐soil‐atmosphere and groundwater‐surface water interactions.

articles.title: Comparative Evaluation of Low‐Flow Estimation Performance in Noah‐MP for Improved Hydrological Modeling Across the United States
articles.titleEn: Comparative Evaluation of Low‐Flow Estimation Performance in Noah‐MP for Improved Hydrological Modeling Across the United States
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Accurately simulating low flows is essential for effective water resource management and ecosystem conservation. This study evaluates five runoff and groundwater configurations in the Noah‐MP land surface model—SIMGM, SIMTOP, Schaake96, BATS, and the newly integrated Groundwater for Ungauged Basins (GrUB)—across 543 minimally disturbed reference basins in the contiguous United States. GrUB represents groundwater discharge using a representative‐hillslope formulation with independently derived watershed‐scale parameters and no basin‐specific streamflow calibration. Model performance was assessed using Kling‐Gupta Efficiency (KGE), Nash‐Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and bias under general and low‐flow conditions, identified by the 80% exceedance flows () and Tennant method (). Results indicate no configuration performed best across all metrics. During low‐flow periods, Schaake96 consistently produced the lowest MAE and bias, while GrUB generally ranked second and outperformed SIMGM, SIMTOP, and BATS under both low‐flow definitions. Over the full simulation period, GrUB showed comparatively strong overall performance and the lowest median bias. Spatially, the five configurations generally overestimated low flows in many central and eastern basins, whereas localized underestimation occurred in portions of the Midwest and western United States. Overall, Schaake96 showed the strongest low‐flow performance, while GrUB provided relatively small low‐flow errors and balanced overall performance using independently derived parameters without basin‐specific streamflow calibration. These results highlight substantial differences among Noah‐MP runoff and groundwater configurations and their representation of low‐flow processes.

articles.title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
articles.titleEn: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
articles.abstract: Wernicke’s area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke’s area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke’s area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

articles.title: Methane outburst driven by magma–sediment interactions at Fentale Volcano detected by satellite
articles.titleEn: Methane outburst driven by magma–sediment interactions at Fentale Volcano detected by satellite
articles.abstract: Magmatic intrusions into sedimentary rocks can release carbon-based greenhouse gases, dominantly methane, and have been linked to rapid changes in past climate. However, modern volcanic systems typically emit very little methane, meaning that appropriate analogues are lacking. Here we report satellite measurements of an outburst of methane and carbon dioxide from a restless but non-erupting volcano in the East African Rift. Following a mega-dyke intrusion in 2025, Fentale Volcano (Ethiopia) released at least 38.2 ± 3.9 kt CH 4 over 3 months and at least 2.9 ± 1.0 MtCO 2 . The peak methane emission rate of 157 ± 41 t h −1 is comparable to major industrial blowouts and approximately four orders of magnitude higher than methane emission rates from other volcanic systems. The emissions coincided with localized ground subsidence and thermal anomalies within Fentale’s caldera. We propose that the intrusion disrupted an impermeable cap beneath which methane, derived from hydrocarbon-rich sediments, was trapped. This single outburst is small compared with annual emissions from natural and anthropogenic sources, but demonstrates an unrecognized source of episodic methane emissions, providing insight into greenhouse gas release from magmatic–sedimentary systems.

articles.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
articles.titleEn: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
articles.abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year −1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year −1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year −1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

articles.title: Climate suitability of East Asian mangroves for nature-based solutions is limited by climate extremes
articles.titleEn: Climate suitability of East Asian mangroves for nature-based solutions is limited by climate extremes
articles.abstract: Mangroves represent distinctive coastal ecosystems that offer ecological benefits, notably through their high carbon sequestration rates. However, their resilience to extreme climate events remains uncertain. Here, we investigated the response of mangroves in East Asia to climate variability by employing the remote-sensing derived Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) as a proxy for canopy greenness. A bootstrapping-based statistical framework was applied to identify vegetation responses associated with extreme climate events and quantify lagged climatic effects. We found East Asian mangrove NDVI variability was strongly influenced by preceding winter temperature and seasonal solar radiation, with distinct lagged responses on seasonal time scales across latitudinal zones. These findings were extrapolated to future projections by the Earth system modelling to assess future climate suitability for existing mangroves and for areas of potential thermal suitability in East Asia, particularly China, South Korea and Japan. While shifts in wintertime isotherms suggest a northward shift in the thermal range of mangroves under global warming, low solar radiation events associated with aerosol emissions under the high-emission SSP3-7.0 scenario could constrain future climatic suitability for mangroves. This study highlights that both temperature-driven opportunities and solar radiation constraints should be integrated into practical planning for future conservation, restoration, and migration as nature-based climate solutions.

articles.title: The SOLCHECK project: An investigation into the imprints of solar variability across multiple timescales
articles.titleEn: The SOLCHECK project: An investigation into the imprints of solar variability across multiple timescales
articles.abstract: The project Solar Contribution to Climate Change on Decadal to Centennial Timescales (SOLCHECK) investigated the influence of solar variability on the atmosphere from the pre-industrial era to the present and future. Variations in solar output ranging from weeks to millennia leave distinct imprints on the climate system. Their assessment is, however, challenging because of limited observations, incomplete representation of feedback processes in climate models, and computational constraints. Using a large ensemble of simulations with advanced chemistry–climate models and realistic solar forcing, SOLCHECK aimed to reduce uncertainties in atmospheric solar imprints and to assess the sensitivity of the atmospheric response across timescales and climate states. One key result is that although the initial radiative and chemical responses to the 11-year solar cycle are consistent across models in the upper tropical stratosphere, a robust assessment of tropospheric and surface solar signatures in northern winter is limited due to the variable impact of the stratospheric polar vortex. SOLCHECK also shows that the climate system responds differently to solar forcing under past, present, and future conditions, with stronger responses in the tropical upper troposphere and Arctic as anthropogenic warming progresses. Moreover, extreme solar storms may substantially reduce stratospheric ozone up to a year, with increases in skin-damaging UV of a few percent at northern subtropical and mid-latitudes in spring/summer.

articles.title: Spatial patterns in indirect effects of human activity on climate, land, and water: comparing top-down and bottom-up clustering approaches
articles.titleEn: Spatial patterns in indirect effects of human activity on climate, land, and water: comparing top-down and bottom-up clustering approaches
articles.abstract: In order to assess the full systemic impact of anthropogenic pressures on climate and land, it is crucial to account for indirect impacts mediated by bio-geophysical processes. These impacts typically display a high spatial heterogeneity. In this study, we systematically compare the ability of top-down and bottom-up clustering approaches to capture the spatial patterns in indirect effects on climate, land, and water. Effect sizes are estimated based on simulations conducted with an offline global spatial vegetation model. Following a top-down approach, we map the resulting global pattern on common natural partitions of the Earth. Cluster validity indices reveal a close alignment between the indirect impacts of land use change on climate and an Earth partition into biomes. In contrast, the indirect impacts of climate- and land use change on surface water runoff are best captured by the Köppen-Geiger climate zones. Adopting a bottom-up approach, we employ multivariate spatially constrained clustering to derive an integrative global partition. Several patches of tropical rainforest on the Indomalayan islands as well as large areas of warm grasslands in Australia are identified as high-impact clusters. The results of this study should be considered illustrative as they are based on only one dynamical vegetation model. Nevertheless, they emphasize the local nature of indirect impacts and elucidate the potential and limitations of both top-down and bottom-up spatial aggregation.

articles.title: Ground-truthing the application of compound-specific stable isotopes of amino acids to planktic foraminifera tests from Santa Barbara Basin
articles.titleEn: Ground-truthing the application of compound-specific stable isotopes of amino acids to planktic foraminifera tests from Santa Barbara Basin
articles.abstract: Planktic foraminifera form shells that are preserved in ocean sediments and are used in a variety of paleoproxy and biostratigraphic applications. However, species-specific ecology can complicate the interpretation of planktic foraminifera-based proxies, and limited options exist for examining the ecology of extinct species. Here we apply test-bound compound-specific stable isotopes of amino acids (CSI-AA) to examine the trophic ecology of extant planktic foraminifera. We measure CSI-AA in planktic foraminifera shells collected in sediment traps from the Santa Barbara Basin, CA, specifically the three most abundant species in this region: Globigerina bulloides , Neogloboquadrina incompta , and Turborotalita quinqueloba . The nitrogen CSI-AA of all three species suggest that planktic foraminifera have metazoan-like metabolisms, and that trophic position estimates using CSI-AA are appropriate for planktic foraminifera. All three species had trophic positions near 2 (primary consumer), with no evidence for mixotrophy or photosymbionts. Carbon CSI-AA, in combination with a Bayesian stable isotope mixing model, indicates that the three species occupied separate niches based on diet. Globigerina bulloides fed opportunistically on all groups of phytoplankton available in Santa Barbara Basin, adjusting its diet with seasonal changes in phytoplankton assemblage. Turborotalita quinqueloba specialized in diatoms but consumed some heterotrophic bacteria and cyanobacteria. Neogloboquadrina incompta consumed primarily heterotrophic bacteria and some dinoflagellates. Our results align with the current understanding of each species' ecology while further defining their niches. Our findings suggest that CSI-AA is a promising tool for understanding the trophic ecology of planktic foraminifera, and we make recommendations for future applications of CSI-AA to fossil specimens.

articles.title: Acidification in coastal waters of Adélie Land, Antarctica (1985–2025)
articles.titleEn: Acidification in coastal waters of Adélie Land, Antarctica (1985–2025)
articles.abstract: Ocean acidification is expected to be particularly severe in Antarctic continental shelves due to enhanced anthropogenic carbon uptake in cold waters in response to rising atmospheric CO 2 , sea-ice retreat, freshening and climate-change feedbacks. Models suggest that undersaturated conditions with respect to aragonite (Ω ar ), a major form of calcium carbonate formed by marine species, could be reached as soon as 2052 for austral winter. Here we present new ocean carbonate system observations from cruises conducted since 2010 in the Adélie Land coastal region in East Antarctica, along with data from a BCG-Argo float and results from a neural network model for the period 1985–2025. The region is a permanent CO 2 sink which was most pronounced since 2006. The CO 2 sink leads to an increase of surface water total CO 2 concentrations ( C T ) (+0.44 ± 0.01 µmolkg-1yr-1) and to a decrease of pH (−0.013 per decade) and Ω ar (−0.035 per decade) for the winter season. The lowest surface Ω ar of 1.2 was observed in winter 2024 from the float data, a critical limit for some marine species such as pteropods. A projection of the C T concentrations in the future, based on observed anthropogenic CO 2 concentrations and emissions scenarios, suggests that aragonite saturation state (Ω ar = 1) will occur in surface waters as soon as 2055 in the Adélie Land region, which is part of a larger area of East Antarctica proposed as a Marine Protected Area by the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources since the early 2010s.
articles.abstractEn: Ocean acidification is expected to be particularly severe in Antarctic continental shelves due to enhanced anthropogenic carbon uptake in cold waters in response to rising atmospheric CO 2 , sea-ice retreat, freshening and climate-change feedbacks. Here we present new ocean carbonate system observations from cruises conducted since 2010 in the Adélie Land coastal region in East Antarctica, along with data from a BCG-Argo float and results from a neural network model for the period 1985–2025. The region is a permanent CO 2 sink which was most pronounced since 2006. The CO 2 sink leads to an increase of surface water total CO 2 concentrations ( C T ) (+0.44 ± 0.01 µmolkg-1yr-1) and to a decrease of pH (−0.013 per decade) and Ω ar (−0.035 per decade) for the winter season. The lowest surface Ω ar of 1.2 was observed in winter 2024 from the float data, a critical limit for some marine species such as pteropods. A projection of the C T concentrations in the future, based on observed anthropogenic CO 2 concentrations and emissions scenarios, suggests that aragonite saturation state (Ω ar = 1) will occur in surface waters as soon as 2055 in the Adélie Land region, which is part of a larger area of East Antarctica proposed as a Marine Protected Area by the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources since the early 2010s.

articles.title: Assessing the contribution of extratropical cyclones to river floods that caused property damage in Quebec, Canada
articles.titleEn: Assessing the contribution of extratropical cyclones to river floods that caused property damage in Quebec, Canada
articles.abstract: In the past few decades, the province of Quebec in eastern Canada has experienced widespread and costly flood events, yet the contribution of extratropical cyclones to these floods remains unquantified. This paper presents a methodology for analysing the contribution of extratropical cyclones (ETCs) to 498 fluvial floods that occurred in watersheds in southern Quebec, Canada, between 1991 and 2020, and highlights key characteristics shared by the 200 flood ETCs (storms that contributed to flooding) identified in the study. This analysis combined reconstituted river outputs, government financial aid claims following flooding, ETC tracks, and precipitation data to identify flood events and their relevant ETCs. ETC contribution was defined as the percentage of rainfall during a search window surrounding each flood event that was associated with the relevant ETCs. Most of these floods occurred in the spring (74.7 %). The majority (72.7 %) of flood events had a high (50 %–75 %) to very high (>75 %) ETC contribution, and only 2.6 % of events (mostly occurring in summer) had a negligible ( Baseline Southern Quebec domain , N =6027). Flood ETCs also spent on average 18.2 h more in the domain and generally tracked over southern Quebec as opposed to over the Atlantic Ocean along the east coast of North America or over northern Quebec like non-flood ETCs. The percentages of financial aid claims allotted to flood ETCs were highly variable. Just five of the 200 flood ETCs were associated with 51.0 % of all financial aid claims filed during the 30-year period, indicating that a high to very high ETC contribution rarely resulted in widespread flooding. The method developed in this study could be applied to other regions or types of storms analysed (e.g. tropical cyclones and mesoscale convective systems) to further our understanding of the atmospheric causes of flooding in northeastern North America.

articles.title: Process diagnostics of snowmelt runoff in global hydrological and land surface models – Part 2: Are more complex models better?
articles.titleEn: Process diagnostics of snowmelt runoff in global hydrological and land surface models – Part 2: Are more complex models better?
articles.abstract: The added value of increased process complexity has long been a central yet unresolved question in hydrological modeling, particularly for snowmelt runoff (SMR), where multiple physical processes interact in complex ways. In this study, we develop a Tree-Based Model Complexity Scoring (TBMCS) method to quantify the complexity of snow-related processes across 13 global hydrological and land surface models. We then systematically revisit the important linkage between model complexity and model performance in three distinct SMR characteristics, i.e., total runoff ( Q sum ), peak flow ( Q max ), and centroid timing (CTQ) of runoff in the snowmelt period. Further, we assess how the basin complexity (as delineated by 1455 snow-dominated basins), forcing difference and calibration status can modulate this linkage. Results show that (1) models differ substantially in their physical process representations, with the largest divergence in melting process treatments, followed by sublimation, interception and rainfall-snowfall partitioning processes. (2) Model performance for Q sum and Q max shows only weak associations with model complexity. Interestingly, we find a positive correlation between snow-process complexity and model performance for CTQ ( r =0.32).
